stem: Epidemiologists tracking the 1918 influenza outbreak in rural districts noted that infection rates did not ______ until quarantine measures had been in place for several weeks: only then did daily case counts begin their steady decline.

choices.why: Reversed: to escalate is to increase in intensity, but the colon points to a 'steady decline,' the opposite direction.
Unsupported: to fluctuate is to shift irregularly up and down, but the passage describes a steady one-directional decline, not variability.
The colon glosses the blank: case counts 'begin their steady decline,' so the blank must mean lessen or decrease.
Fails on precision: to stabilize is to stop changing and hold level, but the counts did not level off—they declined steadily.

stem: In nineteenth-century Britain, imprisonment for unpaid debts was finally ______ by parliamentary statute: the once-routine practice disappeared entirely from the legal system rather than being merely narrowed or reformed.

choices.why: The colon explains the blank: the practice 'disappeared entirely,' so the statute must have formally ended or eliminated it.
Reversed: to reinstate is to restore something previously removed, but the passage says the practice vanished, not that it returned.
Contradicted by the passage: to amend is to alter or reform, and the text explicitly rules out the practice 'being merely... reformed.'
Fails on precision: to regulate is to control or restrict, but the practice was not narrowed—it was eliminated outright.

stem: Facing printing costs that threatened the project, the editors chose to ______ the explorer's two-thousand-page journals, trimming repetitive entries while preserving every major expedition narrative so that a single published volume retained the original's essential arc.

choices.why: Unsupported: to annotate is to add explanatory notes, but the editors were cutting material to reduce costs, not adding commentary.
Reversed: to embellish is to add decorative or elaborative material, the opposite of the trimming the passage describes.
Wrong domain: to censor is to suppress objectionable content, but the cuts here targeted repetition for length and cost, not offensive material.
The clues 'trimming repetitive entries while preserving' the core and fitting a 'single published volume' point to shortening the work—precisely what abridge means.

stem: Medieval mapmakers often traced coastlines in saturated indigo to ______ the boundary between land and sea: the vivid pigment drew the viewer's eye directly to the contour most critical for navigation.

choices.why: Reversed: to obscure is to hide or make unclear, but the pigment made the boundary more visible, not less.
The colon explains the purpose: the pigment 'drew the viewer's eye directly' to the boundary, so the blank must mean emphasize or highlight.
Unsupported: to replicate is to copy or reproduce, and nothing in the passage concerns duplicating the coastline.
Fails on intensity: to exaggerate is to distort beyond truth, but the mapmakers made a real contour more prominent without misrepresenting it.

stem: In early trials of the water-filtration prototype, engineers judged the device's performance ______ though hardly remarkable: it met every minimum safety threshold set by regulators yet fell well short of the efficiency the team had hoped to achieve.

choices.why: The colon supplies the definition: the device 'met every minimum safety threshold' while remaining unremarkable, so it was satisfactory—meeting required standards without exceeding them.
Fails on intensity: exceptional means outstandingly good, which 'hardly remarkable' and 'fell well short' directly contradict.
Reversed: deficient means failing to meet a required standard, but the device satisfied every regulatory threshold.
Unsupported: irrelevant means unrelated to the matter at hand, and the passage evaluates the device's quality, not its pertinence.

stem: Although quantum mechanics is notorious for its forbidding mathematics, the physicist's popular essays render the field's central ideas ______ to general readers: vivid analogies stand in for formal equations, so no specialized training is required.

choices.why: Reversed: esoteric means intelligible only to specialists, but the essays remove the need for specialized training.
Unsupported: indispensable means absolutely necessary, and the passage discusses how easily readers can grasp the ideas, not whether they need them.
The colon gives the clue: analogies replace equations so 'no specialized training is required,' meaning the ideas become easy for anyone to understand.
Fails on precision: familiar means already well known, but the essays make new ideas understandable, not previously encountered.

stem: For Victorian gentlemen, the pocket watch often functioned less as an essential instrument than as a fashionable ______: suspended from a gleaming chain across the waistcoat, it was added to an ensemble chiefly to signal taste and prosperity.

choices.why: Reversed: a staple is a basic, essential item, but the passage explicitly contrasts the watch with an 'essential instrument.'
The contrast 'less as an essential instrument than as' plus 'added to an ensemble' to enhance attractiveness defines an accessory: a nonessential item that makes something more appealing.
Unsupported: an heirloom is an object passed down through generations, and the passage says nothing about inheritance.
Wrong domain: a commodity is a good bought and sold in commerce, but the passage concerns adornment of an outfit, not trade.

stem: Zaha Hadid's design for the Vitra Fire Station drew international ______ upon its completion in 1993: critics lauded its fractured geometry as a bold rethinking of architectural form, and prestigious commissions soon followed.

choices.why: Wrong connotation: notoriety is fame for something bad or scandalous, but the critics' response was admiring, not disapproving.
Fails on precision: scrutiny is close critical examination, which is neutral—the colon specifies that critics 'lauded' the design, not merely studied it.
Reversed: skepticism is doubt, but the passage shows critics praising the work and rewarding it with commissions.
The colon supplies the clue: critics 'lauded' the design and prestigious commissions followed, so the building attracted enthusiastic public praise.

stem: Completing the transcontinental railroad in 1869 was a formidable ______: laborers had blasted tunnels through the granite of the Sierra Nevada and laid nearly two thousand miles of track, finishing a project that many engineers had dismissed as impossible.

choices.why: The clues 'Completing' and 'finishing a project... dismissed as impossible' describe the successful attainment of a difficult goal—an accomplishment.
Reversed in time: an aspiration is a hope not yet realized, but the passage describes work already completed.
Unsupported: a coincidence is an accidental co-occurrence of events, but the railroad resulted from deliberate, arduous labor.
Fails on intensity: a formality is a routine act done for procedure's sake, contradicting 'formidable' and the project's near-impossible difficulty.

stem: In the published correction, the research team took care to ______ the statistical errors that had inflated their original findings, openly conceding what earlier press releases had strenuously minimized.

choices.why: Reversed: to dispute is to contest or deny, but the appositive says the team was 'openly conceding' the errors.
Unsupported: to overstate is to exaggerate, but the team was admitting the errors accurately, not inflating them further.
The phrase 'openly conceding what earlier press releases had... minimized' restates the blank: the team admitted the truth of the errors.
Fails on precision: to lament is to express sorrow or regret, but the passage supports admission of fact, not an expression of grief.

stem: Though the botanist privately doubted the committee's decision to reclassify the rare orchid, she chose to ______ rather than prolong a dispute she could not win, raising no objection when the revised taxonomy was formally adopted.

choices.why: Reversed: to dissent is to voice disagreement, but she raised 'no objection' when the decision was adopted.
Unsupported: to equivocate is to speak ambiguously to avoid commitment, but she made a clear choice to go along, not a vague one.
Fails on precision: to concur is to genuinely agree, but she 'privately doubted' the decision—she accepted it without actually agreeing.
The clues 'privately doubted' yet 'raising no objection' capture acquiescence: reluctantly accepting something without protest.

stem: Perfect pitch was long assumed to be an innate gift, but recent studies suggest the ability can be ______ through intensive ear training, since young students who received systematic instruction in early childhood developed it at strikingly high rates.

choices.why: Reversed: inherited means received genetically at birth, but the contrast with 'innate gift' and the clue 'through intensive ear training' point to learning, not heredity.
The contrast marker 'but' opposes 'innate gift,' and 'through intensive ear training' shows the ability is gained by effort and experience—acquired.
Reversed in direction: forfeited means lost or surrendered, but the students gained the ability rather than losing it.
Unsupported: simulated means imitated or faked, but the students genuinely 'developed' the ability, not a mere imitation of it.

stem: Conservators restoring the Ghent Altarpiece must ______ to protocols established by an international commission: every solvent, brushstroke, and varnish layer is specified in advance, and any deviation requires formal approval.

choices.why: The colon explains the blank: every step 'is specified in advance' and 'any deviation requires formal approval,' so the conservators must strictly follow the protocols.
Reversed: to object to something is to oppose it, but the passage describes compliance with the protocols, not resistance.
Unsupported: to revert to something is to return to an earlier state or practice, and nothing in the passage involves going back to a previous method.
Wrong connotation: to succumb to something is to be overcome by a harmful force or pressure, but the protocols are professional rules to follow, not an overpowering threat.

stem: Ecologists studying alpine wildflowers found that early snowmelt proved ______ for seedlings on south-facing slopes: plants there gained several additional weeks of growing time and produced markedly more seeds than their late-emerging counterparts.

choices.why: Reversed: detrimental means harmful, but the seedlings gained growing time and produced more seeds—clear benefits.
Unsupported: inevitable means unavoidable, and the passage evaluates whether the snowmelt helped the plants, not whether it was certain to occur.
The colon lists the benefits—extra 'growing time' and 'markedly more seeds'—so early snowmelt was favorable and beneficial for these seedlings.
Wrong domain: profitable means yielding financial gain, but the benefits here are biological (growth and seed production), not monetary.

stem: Nineteenth-century landscape architects continued to ______ the creation of expansive public parks, arguing in lectures and civic reports that green space was essential to urban health, even though they had no authority to compel cities to act.

choices.why: Reversed: to oppose is to argue against, but the architects argued that parks were 'essential to urban health'—a case in favor.
The participial clue 'arguing in lectures and civic reports that green space was essential' shows the architects publicly supported and promoted the parks.
Fails on intensity: to mandate is to officially require, but the passage states they 'had no authority to compel cities to act'—they could only urge.
Fails on intensity in the other direction: to tolerate is to passively allow, but the architects actively campaigned through lectures and reports.

stem: Critics found the memoir's final chapters quietly ______: the author's spare, unadorned account of her father's decline moved many reviewers to tears, achieving its emotional force without a trace of melodrama.

choices.why: Reversed: detached means emotionally uninvolved, but chapters that 'moved many reviewers to tears' are the opposite of cold or distant.
Fails on precision: sentimental implies excessive or self-indulgent emotion, which 'spare, unadorned' and 'without a trace of melodrama' explicitly rule out.
Unsupported: humorous means comic or amusing, but the passage describes an account of decline that brought reviewers to tears, not laughter.
The colon gives the clue: the chapters 'moved many reviewers to tears' through genuine 'emotional force,' so they were deeply touching—affecting.

stem: Even as a child, the marine biologist felt a deep, almost instinctive ______: she returned to the same rocky tide pools day after day, crouching for hours, drawn again and again to the small creatures she discovered among the stones.

choices.why: The colon elaborates a natural pull—returning 'day after day,' 'drawn again and again'—so the blank names an instinctive liking or attraction.
Reversed: an aversion is a strong dislike that would drive her away, not draw her back repeatedly.
Rapport is a harmonious mutual understanding between people; it does not describe a person's pull toward a place or wild creatures.
Reversed: detachment is emotional distance or indifference, the opposite of the eager, repeated engagement described.

stem: In negotiations, the firm's new director abandoned the cautious, measured approach of her predecessor; her ______ tactics—making bold demands and refusing to yield an inch—unsettled competitors who had grown comfortable with a gentler style.

choices.why: Reversed: timid means shy and hesitant, contradicting 'bold demands' and 'refusing to yield.'
'Bold demands' and 'refusing to yield an inch,' set against a 'gentler style,' point to forceful, dominating behavior.
Reversed: conciliatory tactics aim to appease and soften conflict, the opposite of the forceful pressure she applies.
Impulsive means acting on sudden whim, but her deliberate 'tactics' are calculated, not rash; nothing marks them as spontaneous.

stem: Peering through his microscope at a drop of pond water, the student identified a single-celled ______: a simple, non-flowering organism that, much like the seaweeds it faintly resembled, harnessed sunlight to manufacture its own food.

choices.why: A fungus absorbs nutrients from other matter and does not photosynthesize, contradicting 'harnessed sunlight to manufacture its own food.'
A bacterium is single-celled but is not a plantlike organism resembling seaweed, which the passage stresses.
The colon defines it as a simple, non-flowering, sunlight-harnessing organism resembling seaweed—precisely an alga.
A mineral is a nonliving inorganic substance, so it cannot be a single-celled organism that resembles seaweed and makes food.

stem: Rather than naming the war directly, the poet chose only to ______ to it, scattering images of broken fences and empty chairs through the verses so that readers would sense the loss without ever being told of it outright.

choices.why: To refer is to mention openly and by name, but the poet deliberately avoids naming the war 'directly.'
Reversed: to attest is to affirm or bear witness openly, the opposite of hinting at something indirectly.
To object is to voice disapproval, a stance the passage never suggests the poet takes.
'Rather than naming... directly' and conveying loss 'without ever being told outright' describe hinting at something indirectly.

stem: The treaty's crucial final clause proved hopelessly ______: one delegation read it as a binding commitment to disarm at once, while the other insisted it required nothing more than a promise of future talks.

choices.why: The colon shows two conflicting yet defensible readings of one clause, so it admits more than one meaning.
Reversed: unequivocal means leaving no doubt and allowing only one interpretation, the opposite of yielding two readings.
Obscure means murky or hard to perceive, but each side reads the clause plainly and confidently—just differently.
Verbose means using too many words; the problem is dual meaning, not length.

stem: Offered a prestigious research post overseas, Mara was seized by ______: thrilled at the honor and eager to prove herself, she nonetheless dreaded leaving the crowded, familiar city and the friends who had shaped her.

choices.why: Elation names intense joy alone, ignoring the dread she simultaneously feels.
'Thrilled... nonetheless dreaded' names two opposing feelings held at once—the core of ambivalence.
Reversed: indifference is an absence of feeling, contradicting her strong reactions on both sides.
Reluctance captures only her dread, not the thrill and eagerness she feels at the same time.

stem: The sanitation commission's reforms were designed not to abolish urban poverty outright but to ______ the daily hardships of tenement dwellers; cleaner water and better ventilation made cramped, difficult lives at least somewhat more bearable.

choices.why: Reversed: to aggravate is to make a bad situation worse, but the reforms make lives 'more bearable.'
To eradicate is to wipe out completely, which the passage explicitly says the reforms were 'not' meant to do to poverty.
Making hardships 'at least somewhat more bearable' is making a bad situation better without removing it.
To chronicle is to record events; it concerns documenting, not improving, conditions.

stem: Before the sculptor imposed any structure on it, the wet clay remained utterly ______, its surface bulging and sagging without a single edge, plane, or discernible form to give it definition.

choices.why: Reversed: symmetrical means evenly and regularly shaped, contradicting a mass with no form at all.
Nebulous means hazy or vague and suits ideas or mist, not a solid clay mass with a definite physical surface.
Reversed: angular means marked by sharp corners and edges, which the phrase 'without a single edge' rules out.
'Without a single edge, plane, or discernible form' and a surface that merely bulges and sags describe something shapeless.

stem: The biologist argued that a bird's wing and an insect's wing, though built from entirely different tissues, are functionally ______: each independently evolved the same solution, a broad surface generating lift, to the shared problem of flight.

choices.why: Arriving at 'the same solution... for flight' from different starting tissues makes the two wings comparable in function.
Identical means exactly alike, contradicted by 'entirely different tissues.'
Reversed: antithetical means directly opposed, the opposite of similar or comparable.
Arbitrary means based on whim rather than reason, which has nothing to do with the wings' likeness in function.

stem: To explain how electric current flows through a circuit, the physics teacher offered a homely ______: the electrons streaming along a wire, she said, are much like water coursing through a pipe, driven forward by pressure.

choices.why: A metaphor calls one thing another outright, but the teacher draws an explicit, explanatory comparison signaled by 'like.'
An explanatory comparison—electrons in a wire are 'like' water in a pipe—offered to clarify is exactly an analogy.
A refutation disproves a claim, but nothing here is being disproved.
Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration for effect, absent from this plain, clarifying comparison.

stem: Critics noted how sharply the architect's late style broke from the soft curves of his early work; his final museum was aggressively ______, all jutting corners and hard-edged planes meeting at severe, deliberate intervals.

choices.why: Reversed: sinuous means winding and curved, the opposite of the sharp corners described and echoing the rejected 'soft curves.'
Jagged means roughly and irregularly notched, but the design shows clean, deliberate geometric angles, not raggedness.
'Jutting corners and hard-edged planes meeting at severe... intervals' describe a form built from sharp angles.
Reversed: rounded means smoothly curved, contradicting the hard edges and jutting corners.

stem: Decades after the border war finally ended, the two mountain villages remained bitterly unreconciled: the deep ______ the other, nursed through generations of remembered wrongs, resurfaced the moment the disputed valley was so much as mentioned.

choices.why: Reversed: affinities are feelings of warm attraction, contradicting 'bitterly unreconciled' and 'remembered wrongs.'
Reversed: sympathies are feelings of compassion or alliance, the opposite of the hostility the passage describes.
Suspicions are wary distrust, milder than the deep, active hostility that 'resurfaced' over remembered wrongs.
'Bitterly unreconciled,' 'remembered wrongs,' and feelings that 'resurfaced' mark deep hostile feelings directed at the other village.

stem: As she prepared the medieval manuscript for its first printed edition, the scholar took care to ______ it thoroughly, adding marginal notes that clarified obscure terms and traced every quotation back to its original source.

choices.why: 'Adding marginal notes that clarified obscure terms' and traced sources is precisely making explanatory notes on a text.
To transcribe is to copy a text out word for word, which adds no explanatory notes of one's own.
Reversed: to censor is to remove objectionable content, the opposite of enriching the text with added notes.
To abridge is to condense or shorten a text, whereas she is adding material to it.

stem: For weeks the readings had held perfectly steady, so when the seismograph traced a single ______ spike, unlike anything the instrument had registered before or since, the researchers first suspected a malfunction rather than a genuine tremor.

choices.why: Reversed: predictable means regular and expected, but the spike is 'unlike anything' recorded before.
A spike 'unlike anything the instrument had registered before or since,' amid steady readings, deviates from the norm.
Erratic means irregular and inconsistent over time, but the passage describes one isolated spike, not ongoing unpredictability.
Reversed: recurrent means happening again and again, contradicting 'a single' spike seen neither before nor since.

stem: Most of the survey's data points clustered neatly along the predicted curve, but one stubborn measurement stood far apart from the rest, a puzzling ______ the astronomers could not dismiss and that ultimately betrayed the presence of an undiscovered planet.

choices.why: A coincidence is a chance co-occurrence, but the passage treats the odd point as a meaningful deviation, not an accident.
A precedent is an earlier case used as a model, irrelevant to a lone measurement that departs from the pattern.
A measurement that 'stood far apart from the rest' of a neat pattern is a deviation from what was expected—an outlier.
Reversed: a norm is the usual standard, the opposite of a point standing far apart from the rest.

stem: Although the two chemists had once collaborated warmly, years of bitter disputes over credit left their relationship openly ______: they now contradicted each other at every conference and pointedly refused to cite each other's published work.

choices.why: Reversed: cordial means warm and friendly, the opposite of the open conflict described.
Reversed: collaborative means cooperative and mutually supportive, contradicting their public contradicting and snubbing.
Competitive means eager to outdo one another, which falls short of the open hostility shown by refusing to cite each other.
Contradicting each other publicly and refusing to acknowledge each other's work shows active opposition and hostility.

stem: Legal historians regard the medieval guild not as a mere curiosity but as a direct ______ of the modern trade union: centuries before industrialization, guilds already negotiated wages, regulated training, and shielded members from arbitrary dismissal.

choices.why: The colon explains that guilds performed union-like functions 'centuries before industrialization,' so the blank must name a thing that existed earlier and prefigured what came later.
Reversed: a successor comes after what it replaces, but the passage states that guilds preceded trade unions by centuries.
Reversed: a byproduct is something produced incidentally by another thing, which would make the guild an outgrowth of the union rather than its forerunner.
A counterpart is a parallel equivalent existing alongside something else; nothing in the passage suggests guilds and unions coexisted—one preceded the other.

stem: Margaret Mead's fieldwork in Samoa helped establish ______ as a discipline that joins intimate, long-term observation of a living community's kinship customs and rituals with broader questions about how human cultures develop and diverge.

choices.why: Too specific in the wrong direction: archaeology studies past societies through material remains such as artifacts and ruins, but Mead observed a living community directly.
The appositive after 'discipline' describes the study of human societies, customs, and cultural development—exactly what anthropology is.
Too specific: linguistics is the study of language alone, whereas the passage describes research into kinship, ritual, and cultural development generally.
Physiology concerns the functioning of living organisms' bodies; nothing in the passage involves biological processes rather than cultural ones.

stem: Because storm surges tend to follow well-documented patterns of wind and tide, forecasters can now ______ coastal flooding many hours before it begins, giving low-lying towns precious time to move residents and equipment to higher ground.

choices.why: To prevent is to stop something from happening, but the passage says the flooding still 'begins'; the forecasters only give advance warning.
Reversed in time: to recall is to remember something past, while the passage is about foreseeing an event that has not yet occurred.
The phrase 'many hours before it begins,' supported by 'well-documented patterns,' shows the forecasters predict the flooding in advance—the meaning of anticipate.
To observe is to watch something as it happens, which contradicts 'before it begins'; the passage describes prediction, not eyewitness monitoring.

stem: ______ a rush of orders once the celebrated critic's review appeared, the small press printed three times its usual run and hired seasonal staff—preparations that proved prescient when the novel sold out within a week.

choices.why: Reversed in time: recalling means remembering something past, but the rush of orders had not yet happened when the press prepared for it.
Reversed: dismissing means rejecting something as unimportant; a press that dismissed the coming demand would not have tripled its print run.
Witnessing means seeing an event occur, but the press acted before the review appeared and before any orders arrived.
The press prepared in advance for a surge that later materialized—'preparations that proved prescient'—so the blank must mean expecting and readying for something.

stem: Hoping to ______ the restive frontier nobles, the young king granted them tax exemptions and seats on his royal council; the concessions bought a fragile peace that lasted nearly a decade.

choices.why: The king offers concessions and the result is 'a fragile peace,' so the blank must mean pacify or satisfy the discontented nobles.
Reversed: to provoke is to stir up anger or rebellion, the opposite of what concessions that 'bought a fragile peace' would do.
To suppress is to put down by force or authority, but the king used generous concessions, not coercion, to calm the nobles.
To emulate is to imitate in hopes of matching someone; nothing suggests the king wanted to copy the nobles rather than calm them.

stem: Reviewers rushed to ______ the architect's design for the city's new library, citing its daylight-filled reading rooms and its deference to the surrounding historic district as proof that civic buildings can be at once practical and inspiring.

choices.why: Reversed: to condemn is to denounce strongly, but the reviewers cite the design's virtues as 'proof' of its success.
The reviewers point to the design's merits as proof that it is 'practical and inspiring,' so the blank must mean praise enthusiastically.
Wrong intensity: to tolerate is to put up with something grudgingly, far weaker than the enthusiastic endorsement the reviewers' 'proof' language conveys.
To scrutinize is to examine closely and neutrally, but the reviewers have already reached an emphatically favorable verdict.

stem: Though the mathematical model was devised to describe how vehicles merge on crowded highways, its equations proved equally ______ to pedestrian movement: stadium planners now use the same formulas to design exits that ease congestion after large events.

choices.why: Too broad a claim: the same formulas are used, but calling the equations 'identical to pedestrian movement' overstates and misstates the relationship, which is one of relevance, not sameness.
Reversed: the colon shows planners actually use the formulas for pedestrians, so the model is pertinent, not beside the point.
The colon explains that planners 'use the same formulas' for crowds, showing the model is relevant to—can be applied to—the new domain.
Detrimental means harmful; the passage says the formulas 'ease congestion,' describing a benefit, not damage.

stem: Before the museum could insure the newly donated canvas, specialists spent weeks ______ it—comparing its brushwork with authenticated works, testing pigment samples, and consulting auction records to fix a defensible estimate of its worth.

choices.why: Restoring means repairing to a former condition, but the activities listed are all forms of examination and valuation, not repair.
Reversed: discarding means throwing away as worthless, yet the museum is preparing to insure the canvas and establish its value.
Admiring means regarding with aesthetic pleasure; the passage describes a systematic, evidence-based valuation, not appreciation.
The dash introduces the methods used 'to fix a defensible estimate of its worth,' the defining activity of appraising—assessing value.

stem: The composer's private notation is so idiosyncratic that even devoted scholars admit they cannot fully ______ his intentions: entire passages of the late quartets remain open to sharply conflicting interpretations.

choices.why: The colon shows that his intentions cannot be settled—interpretations conflict—so the blank must mean grasp or understand.
Too narrow: transcribing is copying notation into another form, but the difficulty described is understanding meaning, not recopying symbols.
Reversed: to dismiss is to reject as unworthy of attention, yet these 'devoted scholars' are laboring to understand the works, not brush them aside.
To endorse is to declare approval; the passage concerns comprehension of the composer's intentions, and approval is never at issue.

stem: Workshop ledgers from Renaissance Florence reveal that most painters began not as independent masters but as ______: adolescents bound to a senior artist for years of grinding pigments, preparing panels, and copying drawings before accepting commissions of their own.

choices.why: Reversed role: a patron commissions and finances art, but the passage describes beginners performing menial tasks to learn the craft.
The colon defines the role—young people 'bound to a senior artist' for years of training tasks—which is precisely what an apprentice is.
A connoisseur is an expert judge of quality; that implies refined mastery, contradicting adolescents still learning to grind pigments.
A rival is a competitor, but the relationship described is instruction and service under a master, not competition with one.

stem: When Alfred Wegener first proposed continental drift, geologists ridiculed the idea; only decades later, once studies of seafloor spreading supplied a plausible mechanism, did the theory finally win the ______ of the scientific establishment.

choices.why: Reversed: derision means mocking scorn—the initial reaction the sentence explicitly contrasts with what the theory 'finally' won.
Notoriety is fame for something bad; the arc of the sentence moves from ridicule toward acceptance, not toward disrepute.
The contrast between early ridicule and what the theory later 'won' requires a word meaning approval or praise—approbation.
Scrutiny is close, neutral examination; the theory had been examined all along, and 'win' signals a favorable verdict, not mere attention.

stem: Statisticians warn that no test is universally valid: a technique ______ for large, normally distributed samples can produce badly misleading conclusions when researchers use it on the small, skewed data sets common in field ecology.

choices.why: Too strong: obligatory means required by rule, but the passage claims only that the technique suits certain data, not that anyone must use it.
Reversed: detrimental means harmful, yet the technique works well for large samples and misleads only when transferred to the wrong data.
Arbitrary means chosen at random without reason; the passage describes a principled match between technique and sample type, not a random one.
The contrast—valid for one kind of sample, misleading for another—turns on suitability, so the blank must mean fitting for a particular situation.

stem: With no complete census surviving from the fourteenth century, historians can only ______ the population of medieval London, piecing together tax rolls, parish registers, and grain-import records to arrive at a defensible range rather than a firm count.

choices.why: The phrase 'a defensible range rather than a firm count' signals an estimate close to but not exactly the true figure—the meaning of approximate.
To verify is to confirm as exactly true, but with no census surviving there is no precise figure to confirm—only fragmentary evidence to estimate from.
Too exact: tabulating implies counting items precisely into totals, which 'range rather than a firm count' explicitly rules out.
To exaggerate is to overstate deliberately; the historians aim at a 'defensible' figure, the opposite of inflating it.

stem: The treatises of medieval alchemists are notoriously ______: written in invented symbols and deliberately coded language, they were intelligible only to initiated practitioners and continue to resist confident interpretation by modern scholars.

choices.why: Reversed: accessible means easily understood, but the texts were 'intelligible only to initiated practitioners' and still baffle scholars.
The colon explains that the texts were coded so that only initiates could read them—known to few and mysterious, the core meaning of arcane.
The treatises are indeed old, but obsolete means outdated and no longer useful, which does not explain why only initiates could read them.
Verbose means using too many words; the difficulty described is deliberate secrecy and coding, not wordiness.

stem: The nineteenth-century survey of the Andes proved ______: crews hauled fragile instruments over unmapped passes, endured weeks of freezing storms, and re-measured entire baselines by hand whenever landslides destroyed their markers.

choices.why: Futile means producing no result; the passage shows the work was punishing, but nothing indicates the survey failed or was pointless.
Too narrow: monotonous means dull through sameness, but hauling instruments over unmapped passes amid storms describes strain and danger, not boredom.
The colon lists grueling physical demands—hauling, enduring storms, re-measuring by hand—so the blank must mean extremely difficult and strenuous.
Lucrative means highly profitable; the passage says nothing about money, only about the labor the survey required.

stem: Critics eventually recognized that the memoirist's disarming frankness was itself a calculated ______: by freely confessing trivial faults, she steered readers away from scrutinizing the book's far larger fabrications.

choices.why: Reversed: a blunder is a careless mistake, but the passage calls the tactic 'calculated' and shows it worked as intended.
A courtesy is a polite gesture; nothing in the passage concerns politeness—the frankness served to conceal deception.
She did disclose minor faults, but the sentence's point is that the openness was a deceptive design, which 'disclosure' fails to capture.
The colon reveals a cunning scheme—confessing small faults to hide 'far larger fabrications'—so the blank must mean a clever trick used to deceive.

stem: Guild records from fourteenth-century Bruges show that before earning the title of master, a ______ was required to spend nearly a decade perfecting handcraft techniques—hammering silver, cutting stone, or binding books—under the scrutiny of the town's most accomplished practitioners.

choices.why: The dash introduces skilled manual crafts—hammering silver, cutting stone, binding books—so the blank must name a skilled worker who makes things by hand.
Too general: a laborer is anyone who does physical work, missing the specialized, mastered craft skill the decade of training implies.
A merchant buys and sells goods; the passage describes making objects by hand, not trading them.
A patron financially supports craftspeople or the arts; nothing in the passage involves funding rather than practicing the craft.

stem: Under the 1867 confederation scheme, no amendment to the colonial charter could take effect until every provincial delegation had granted its formal ______; a single delegation's refusal, however grudging, was enough to stall reform for years.

choices.why: Reversed: dissent means disagreement, which is what the contrasting clause about "refusal" describes, not what the charter requires delegations to grant.
The semicolon contrasts the blank with "refusal," so the blank must mean agreement or approval—what each delegation must grant for an amendment to take effect.
Too strong: acclaim is enthusiastic public praise, but the charter requires only approval, which the passage suggests could even be given grudgingly.
Scrutiny is close, critical examination; the passage concerns authorization of amendments, not their inspection.

stem: In a 1912 address, Alfred Wegener boldly ______ that the continents had once formed a single landmass, a claim he defended without hesitation even as prominent geologists dismissed the mechanism he proposed for their drift.

choices.why: Reversed: to concede is to admit something reluctantly under pressure, but Wegener is confidently advancing a claim, not yielding to opponents.
Wrong manner: to insinuate is to hint at something indirectly and slyly, but "boldly" and "without hesitation" describe an open, direct declaration.
The cues "boldly" and "a claim he defended without hesitation" show a confident declaration, which is exactly what asserted means.
To reiterate is to state something again, but the passage mentions no earlier declaration for Wegener to repeat.

stem: Whereas her predecessor rarely voiced objections during negotiations, the new ambassador adopted an ______ approach, stating her government's positions plainly and pressing counterparts for direct answers while still maintaining a courteous, professional tone.

choices.why: Reversed: acquiescent means passively accepting without protest, which matches the timid predecessor, not the ambassador who presses for answers.
Too strong: aggressive implies hostility or combativeness, which the "courteous, professional tone" explicitly rules out.
Obstinate means stubbornly refusing to change one's position; the passage describes plain, confident speaking, not inflexibility.
The contrast with a predecessor who "rarely voiced objections," plus "stating positions plainly" while staying courteous, defines a confident, self-assured style.

stem: Skeptics had long derided the goal of eradicating the disease as a fantasy, but after vaccination campaigns eliminated it from three continents in a single decade, public health officials began describing global eradication as genuinely ______.

choices.why: Too strong: inevitable means certain to happen, but the campaigns' success shows only that the goal can be reached, not that it is guaranteed.
Reversed: quixotic means hopelessly impractical, which restates the skeptics' "fantasy" view that the new evidence overturns.
Overstates the case: decade-long vaccination campaigns show the goal takes enormous work; achievable does not mean easy.
The contrast marker "but" pivots from "fantasy" to evidence of real progress, so the blank must mean achievable—capable of being reached.

stem: Charred grain stores, loom weights, and dozens of clay seals unearthed at the site ______ to a thriving textile economy: such artifacts could only have accumulated where weaving and trade were sustained for generations.

choices.why: The colon explains that the artifacts "could only have accumulated" under sustained weaving and trade, so they serve as evidence that confirms the economy existed.
Too weak: to allude is to hint at something indirectly, but the passage presents the artifacts as decisive proof, not a vague suggestion.
Reversed: to object to something is to express opposition to it, the opposite of providing supporting evidence.
To succumb is to yield to an overpowering force or temptation; artifacts confirming a historical claim have nothing to do with surrender.

stem: Rather than collapsing after any single crisis, the rural school district was weakened by steady ______: every year a few more veteran teachers resigned than the district could replace, until entire departments had quietly hollowed out.

choices.why: Wrong pace: an exodus is a sudden mass departure, but the passage stresses gradual, year-by-year losses rather than one dramatic event.
The colon defines the blank—staff numbers gradually shrinking as resignations outpace replacements—which is precisely attrition, a slow reduction or weakening.
Reversed: recruitment is the gaining of new staff, the opposite of the steady losses that hollowed out departments.
Stagnation means standing still without change, but the district is actively shrinking, not merely failing to grow.

stem: In most spiral galaxies, the arms trail behind the direction of rotation; NGC 4622, whose outer arms appear to wind forward instead, is therefore considered ______—an exception that has prompted astronomers to revisit their models of galactic dynamics.

choices.why: Defective implies a flaw or malfunction; the galaxy departs from the usual pattern but is not described as broken or damaged.
Reversed: representative means typical of the group, contradicting both "instead" and the appositive "an exception."
The contrast between "most spiral galaxies" and NGC 4622's opposite-winding arms, capped by the appositive "an exception," requires a word meaning not conforming to the usual pattern.
Archaic means ancient or old-fashioned; the passage concerns the galaxy's unusual structure, not its age.

stem: Because the provincial museum's permanent holdings were too sparse to fill its new wing, curators negotiated long-term loans from private collectors to ______ the collection without straining the acquisition budget.

choices.why: Reversed: to curtail is to cut back, but holdings "too sparse to fill" the wing need expansion, not reduction.
To supplant is to replace something entirely; the borrowed works are added alongside the permanent holdings, not substituted for them.
To appraise is to assess the monetary value of something; the passage concerns enlarging the collection, not valuing it.
The clue "too sparse to fill its new wing" shows the collection needs enlarging, and loans that add works without new purchases augment—increase—it.

stem: During the 1848 uprising in Paris, insurgents tore up paving stones and overturned carts to assemble a makeshift ______ across the boulevard, a hastily piled obstruction that halted cavalry charges for nearly two days.

choices.why: Wrong register: a rampart is a permanent defensive embankment built into a fortification, not an improvised pile of stones and carts blocking a street.
Reversed: a thoroughfare is a route for passage, the opposite of an obstruction that halts movement.
A garrison is a body of troops stationed in a town, not a physical structure that can be piled up from stones and carts.
The appositive "a hastily piled obstruction that halted cavalry charges" defines the blank as a makeshift barrier blocking the street.

stem: The essayist's breezy, conversational prose ______ the labor behind it: drafts in her archive reveal that each seemingly offhand paragraph was rewritten a dozen times over several months.

choices.why: The colon exposes a contrast between appearance and reality—effortless-seeming prose masking painstaking revision—so the blank must mean gives a false impression of.
Reversed: to betray a feeling or fact is to inadvertently reveal it, but the breezy prose hides the labor rather than exposing it.
To commemorate is to honor the memory of something; the prose conceals the revision process rather than celebrating it.
To epitomize is to be a perfect example of something, but casual-seeming prose is not an example of heavy labor—it misrepresents it.

stem: Economic historians portray Duluth as a clear ______ the 1870 rail link: within a decade of the line's completion, the town's grain shipments had increased twentyfold and its population had more than tripled.

choices.why: Reversed: a casualty of something is harmed by it, but the colon details dramatic gains, not damage.
The colon lists advantages that followed the rail link—shipments up twentyfold, population tripled—so the town is a recipient of the link's benefits.
An architect of something designs or creates it; the passage shows the town receiving the link's effects, not building the railway.
A precursor of something comes before it, but the town's growth followed the line's completion rather than preceding it.

stem: Contemporaries regarded the industrialist as unusually ______: at his own expense he built workers' housing with running water, endowed a hospital and schools, and provided pensions decades before the law required any such provision.

choices.why: Shrewd means clever and calculating in practical matters; the passage catalogs voluntary generosity, not business cunning.
Too narrow: lenient means mild in punishing or enforcing rules, but the acts described are charitable gifts, not relaxed discipline.
The colon lists charitable acts performed "at his own expense" and beyond legal obligation, marking the industrialist as kind and generous.
Ostentatious means showy in order to impress; nothing in the passage suggests the motive was display rather than workers' welfare.

stem: Reviewers rejected the study's conclusions about national reading habits as ______, noting that the researchers had surveyed only affluent urban households and had therefore given one segment of the population disproportionate weight.

choices.why: Reversed: comprehensive means covering everything, but the survey's flaw is that it covered only one narrow slice of the population.
Surveying "only affluent urban households" and giving one group "disproportionate weight" describes an unfair tilt toward one segment—precisely what biased means.
Subjective means based on personal feelings rather than evidence; the flaw described is a skewed sample, not reliance on opinion.
Obsolete means out of date; the passage says nothing about the study's timing or its methods being superseded.

stem: Before the auction, conservators examined the Renaissance panel under raking light for any ______—a speck of discoloration, a faint scuff, a pinpoint of flaking paint—since even a slight surface imperfection could lower the work's value considerably.

choices.why: The dashes list tiny marks, and "slight surface imperfection" glosses the blank exactly: a small flaw that spoils appearance.
Too severe: a fissure is a major crack or split, but the passage concerns minute surface marks like specks and scuffs.
An embellishment is a decorative addition meant to beautify, not a defect that lowers a work's value.
Examiners might also look for a signature, but the items listed are flaws that reduce value, not marks of authorship.

stem: Critics were struck less by the anthology's insight into any single tradition than by its ______: the volume gathers poems from five continents, spans eight centuries, and moves among dozens of forms and dialects.

choices.why: Reversed: brevity means shortness, but the colon emphasizes how expansively the volume ranges across places, eras, and forms.
Precision failure: depth is thorough treatment of a single area, which the passage explicitly sets aside with "less by... any single tradition."
The colon catalogs range—five continents, eight centuries, dozens of forms—so the blank must mean wide extent or scope.
Novelty means newness or originality; the critics praise the collection's range, not its inventiveness.

stem: A historian studying ancient trade gathered pottery fragments, coins, and shipwreck records to ______ her claim that two distant civilizations had maintained regular contact; each new artifact added weight to a thesis that skeptical colleagues had once dismissed outright.

choices.why: The clue that each artifact 'added weight' to a once-dismissed thesis signals that the evidence is meant to support and strengthen the claim.
Reversed direction: to undermine is to weaken, but the artifacts reinforce the claim.
To embellish is to add decorative or exaggerated detail; the passage describes strengthening a claim with evidence, not ornamenting it.
To summarize is merely to condense; it says nothing about lending support, which the accumulating evidence does.

stem: To reduce delays at the crowded central interchange, city planners designed a ring road that would ______ the downtown core entirely, allowing freight trucks to reach the port without ever entering the congested grid of streets.

choices.why: Reversed: to traverse is to pass directly through, but the road is meant to route trucks around the core.
The phrase 'without ever entering the congested grid' shows the road is built to go around and avoid the downtown core.
To obstruct is to block; the plan clears a path rather than blocking one, contradicting the goal.
To monitor is to observe; the road routes traffic around the center, not watch over it.

stem: When the new wing of the natural history museum opened, curators marveled at how ______ its central hall was: the vaulted space could hold a reconstructed whale skeleton, a suspended aircraft, and hundreds of visitors at once without ever feeling crowded.

choices.why: Too narrow: lofty refers to height alone, but the clue emphasizes the hall's total holding capacity, not merely its tallness.
Reversed: cramped means confined and short of space, the opposite of a hall that never feels crowded.
The detail that the hall holds huge objects and hundreds of people 'without feeling crowded' points to a space that is roomy and spacious.
Ornate describes lavish decoration, not size; the passage is concerned with how much the hall can hold.

stem: From her very first note, the young cellist seemed to ______ the entire concert hall; listeners sat motionless and utterly absorbed, unwilling even to shift in their seats until the final chord had faded into silence.

choices.why: Too weak: to amuse is to provide mild diversion, not the rapt, spellbound absorption the audience displays.
Reversed: to bore is to make listless, but the listeners are riveted and enthralled.
To unsettle is to make uneasy; the audience is entranced, not disturbed.
The image of motionless, utterly absorbed listeners shows the cellist charms and mesmerizes the hall.

stem: During the three-year expedition, the botanists set out to ______ every plant species in the valley, recording each one's location, height, and flowering season in a meticulously ordered register that others could later consult.

choices.why: The detail of recording each species in 'a meticulously ordered register' matches making a systematic list or record.
Too narrow: to tally is merely to count totals, but the botanists record detailed descriptive information, not just numbers.
To uproot is to pull plants up; the botanists document the plants, not remove them.
Reversed: to overlook is to fail to notice, the opposite of carefully recording every species.

stem: Historians often point to the assassination as the ______ for the wider conflict: although tensions had simmered for decades, that single event set in motion the alliances and mobilizations that plunged the continent into war.

choices.why: Reversed: an aftermath is a consequence that follows, but the event is described as what set the war in motion.
The phrase 'set in motion' the events leading to war identifies the assassination as the trigger that precipitated the conflict.
A precedent is an earlier case that guides later ones; nothing suggests the event served as a model, only that it ignited the war.
A hindrance impedes; the assassination advances the conflict rather than obstructing it.

stem: Every ten years the government conducts a nationwide ______, sending workers to record how many people live in each household so that legislative seats and public funds can be apportioned fairly across regions.

choices.why: A referendum is a public vote on a specific question, not a count of how many people live in each household.
Too narrow: a poll samples the opinions of a subset, whereas the passage describes a complete tally of the whole population.
Recording how many people live in each household nationwide is precisely an official count or survey of the population.
An audit is an examination of financial records, not a population count, so it falls outside the passage's domain.

stem: When the graduate student presented data that flatly contradicted the long-accepted model, she effectively ______ the theory that had guided the field for decades, forcing senior researchers to defend assumptions they had never before been asked to justify.

choices.why: Reversed: to endorse is to approve, but the student's contradictory data disputes the theory rather than backing it.
Too narrow: to revise is to alter or edit; the student calls the theory's validity into question, she does not amend it.
To illustrate is to give supporting examples; the passage shows her contesting the theory, not exemplifying it.
Presenting contradictory data that forces researchers to defend their assumptions shows she questioned and disputed the theory's validity.

stem: The zoologist argued that the crescent marking above each eye was the defining ______ of the species: no closely related population displayed it, so the marking alone allowed field researchers to distinguish the animals at a glance.

choices.why: A defining quality unique to the species that lets researchers tell it apart is exactly a distinctive feature or trait.
Too narrow: an anomaly is a deviation or exception, but the marking is a consistent, defining quality of every member of the species.
A quirk is a minor, incidental peculiarity, not the species-defining feature the passage emphasizes.
A habitat is the environment where an animal lives, which is unrelated to a physical marking used for identification.

stem: The ______ spent months arranging every leap and turn of the ballet, deciding exactly where each dancer would stand and how the ensemble would move together before the company ever set foot on the rehearsal stage.

choices.why: A composer arranges music, not the physical movement of dancers, so the role is in the wrong domain.
Designing every leap, turn, and position of the dancers is precisely the work of the person who composes the sequence of dance movements.
A conductor leads the orchestra's musicians; the passage concerns arranging the dancers' steps, not directing the music.
Too broad: a director oversees a whole production, but the passage specifies designing the dance movements in particular.

stem: The veteran diplomat was known for her ______: before responding to any proposal she weighed every possible consequence, consulted her advisers, and chose her words so deliberately that opponents could rarely find fault with them.

choices.why: Reversed: impulsiveness is acting hastily without reflection, the opposite of weighing every consequence beforehand.
Eloquence is fluent, persuasive speech; the passage stresses careful deliberation before speaking, not verbal polish itself.
Weighing every consequence and choosing words with great care before acting describes caution and carefulness exactly.
Too narrow: vigilance is watchful alertness to danger, whereas the passage describes deliberative caution before acting.

stem: The novelist portrays the nervous apprentice ______ fumbling with the delicate instruments, dropping one tool after another and knocking a glass beaker from the bench as his trembling hands refused to cooperate.

choices.why: Reversed: gracefully means with ease and elegance, contradicting the fumbling and dropping the passage describes.
To act deliberately is to act on purpose, but the mishaps stem from trembling, uncontrolled hands, not intention.
Too narrow: hastily stresses speed, but the passage emphasizes gracelessness and lack of control, not how fast he moves.
Fumbling, dropping tools, and knocking over a beaker with uncooperative hands is the very picture of acting awkwardly and ungracefully.

stem: Over millions of years, the scattered particles of dust and gas orbiting the young star began to ______, gradually drawing together under the pull of gravity until they formed the solid cores of the first planets.

choices.why: Particles 'drawing together' under gravity to form planetary cores describes them uniting and combining into a single mass.
Reversed: to disperse is to scatter apart, the opposite of drawing together into planets.
Too narrow: to condense is to grow denser or turn from gas to liquid, not to merge separate particles into larger bodies.
To fluctuate is to shift back and forth irregularly; the passage describes steady merging, not variation.

stem: After the new captain introduced shared goals and open communication, the once-fractured squad developed a striking sense of ______: players trusted one another, moved as a single unit, and no longer pursued personal glory at the team's expense.

choices.why: Reversed: rivalry is internal competition and conflict, the opposite of players who now trust each other and move as one.
Mutual trust and players 'moving as a single unit' rather than seeking personal glory captures unity and solidarity.
Too narrow: conformity is uniformity of behavior or compliance, not the mutual bonding and shared purpose the passage describes.
A hierarchy is a system of ranking; the passage concerns unity among equals, not a chain of authority.

stem: The researchers cautioned that the apparent link between the two rising trends was probably ______: with so many variables tracked over the decade, some pairs were bound to rise together by chance alone, with no real connection between them.

choices.why: Reversed: deliberate means intentional, but the passage attributes the link to random chance, not design.
Reversed: causal implies one trend truly produces the other, the very connection the researchers say is absent.
The explanation that the pairing arose 'by chance alone, with no real connection' matches something accidental and unplanned.
Anomalous means abnormal or deviating; the passage says such chance pairings are expected, not unusual.

stem: The breakthrough vaccine emerged not from a single laboratory but from close ______ among dozens of institutions on three continents, each freely sharing its data, samples, and expertise in pursuit of one common goal.

choices.why: Reversed: competition is rivalry, but the institutions freely share resources toward a shared aim.
Too narrow: coordination is the logistical arranging of activities, not the joint creative effort of sharing data and expertise.
Reversed: isolation means working separately, the opposite of institutions working jointly across continents.
Many institutions sharing data and expertise toward a common goal is exactly a cooperative effort or joint partnership.

stem: When an independent panel re-examined the disputed safety report, the reviewers found the engineer's warnings so thoroughly documented that they could only ______: every member accepted her conclusion that the existing measures were inadequate.

choices.why: The clause 'every member accepted her conclusion' signals unanimous agreement, so the blank must mean to agree or accord.
To demur is to raise objections or hesitate, the reverse of the unanimous acceptance the passage describes.
To waver is to be indecisive, but the reviewers are said to accept the conclusion firmly.
To digress is to wander off topic, which has nothing to do with the reviewers' shared verdict.

stem: Early ecologists assumed the rare orchid could flourish almost anywhere, but later fieldwork showed that its dependence on a single soil fungus forced botanists to ______ their search to the few shaded ravines where that fungus actually thrives.

choices.why: To broaden is to widen the scope, the opposite of narrowing the search to a few ravines.
'To the few shaded ravines where that fungus thrives' narrows the range, so the blank must mean to restrict or limit.
To catalogue is to list systematically; the sentence is about restricting where they look, not recording it.
To relinquish is to give up entirely, but the botanists continue searching in a smaller area.

stem: For decades physicians believed the fever was ______ tropical ports, appearing only in towns where ships from the equator docked; the later discovery of cases deep in the arid interior forced them to abandon that comfortable assumption.

choices.why: To be exempt from something is to be free of it, but the fever supposedly occurred in the ports, not spared from them.
'Derived from' names an origin, yet the passage stresses where the disease appeared, not where it came from.
'Appearing only in towns where ships docked' marks a strict boundary, so the fever was limited or restricted to those ports.
'Typical of' means characteristic, but it fails to capture the exclusivity that 'only' establishes.

stem: A recurring error in introductory reasoning is to treat two distinct relationships as though they were a single one; students who ______ correlation and causation assume that because two trends happen to rise together, one of them must be producing the other.

choices.why: To distinguish is to tell things apart, the opposite of treating them as a single relationship.
To isolate is to set one thing apart from others, again the reverse of merging the two concepts.
To quantify is to measure in numbers, which is unrelated to blurring two ideas together.
'Treat two distinct relationships as though they were a single one' defines the blank as to merge or confuse them.

stem: The regulatory agency does not reward a new drug for its novelty; before approval, each compound must ______ the strict safety thresholds printed in the pharmacopeia, matching every published benchmark for purity and dosage.

choices.why: 'Matching every published benchmark' shows the compound must comply with or adhere to the thresholds.
To deviate from a standard is to depart from it, the opposite of matching every benchmark.
To detract from is to diminish; nothing suggests the drug reduces the thresholds.
'Account for' means to explain or make up a portion of, not to satisfy a required standard.

stem: The astronomer was careful to label her proposal precisely: lacking any direct observation of the distant planet's interior, she presented her account of its composition as ______, a plausible guess awaiting the measurements a future probe might one day supply.

choices.why: Certainty implies established fact, but the astronomer explicitly lacks direct observation.
'A plausible guess awaiting measurements' and 'lacking any direct observation' define the blank as speculation or a guess.
Consensus means broad agreement among people, which the passage never mentions.
Corroboration is confirming evidence, the reverse of an unverified guess.

stem: The historian resisted the temptation to view the two uprisings as isolated events; combing through private letters and shipping records, she traced a clear ______ between them, showing how organizers in one city had corresponded with and inspired those in the other.

choices.why: A divide is a separation, the opposite of the link the correspondence reveals.
A coincidence implies no real relationship, yet the letters show one group deliberately inspired the other.
'Organizers had corresponded with and inspired' the others establishes a relationship or link between the events.
A hierarchy is a ranked ordering, which the passage never establishes between the two cities.

stem: Museums frequently consult her before any major acquisition: decades spent studying brushwork, varnish, and pigment have made her a genuine ______, able to tell a master's own hand from a skilled imitation at a single glance.

choices.why: A novice is an inexperienced beginner, the opposite of someone with decades of expert judgment.
A custodian is a caretaker of property, not necessarily an expert judge of artistic quality.
A patron financially supports the arts, which is unrelated to the discerning taste the passage emphasizes.
'Decades studying pigment' and telling a master from an imitation define an expert judge in matters of taste.

stem: Unlike his brusque predecessor, the new supervisor was unfailingly ______: he learned each employee's personal constraints, adjusted deadlines whenever someone faced a family emergency, and asked after their well-being before handing out any new assignment.

choices.why: Learning employees' constraints and asking after their well-being shows the supervisor is thoughtful and attentive to others.
Indifferent means uncaring, the reverse of a supervisor attentive to each person's needs.
Gregarious means sociable and fond of company, which is not the same as being caring toward others.
Meticulous describes careful attention to detail in work, not kindness toward people.

stem: The pathologist stopped short of asserting certainty, observing only that the pattern of injuries was ______ a fall from a great height: nothing in the physical evidence contradicted that explanation, and every fracture matched the distribution such a fall would produce.

choices.why: 'At odds with' means in conflict, but the evidence is said to contradict nothing about the fall.
'Nothing contradicted that explanation' and 'every fracture matched' show the injuries were in agreement or harmony with a fall.
'Irrelevant to' means unrelated, yet the injuries directly support the fall theory.
'Responsible for' reverses the causal direction; the fall caused the injuries, not the other way around.

stem: The male bird's plumage is anything but subtle; set against the muted green of the canopy, its scarlet crest is so ______ that predators and potential mates alike can pick the bird out from a considerable distance.

choices.why: Drab means dull and unnoticeable, the opposite of a scarlet crest visible from far away.
Fleeting refers to brief duration, but the passage concerns how visible the crest is, not how long it lasts.
'Spot it from a considerable distance' and 'anything but subtle' define the blank as clearly visible.
Fragile means easily broken, which is irrelevant to how easily the crest is seen.

stem: Working only from scattered fossil fragments, the paleontologist set out to ______ a complete model of the extinct reptile, fitting each recovered bone into a supporting scaffold that would eventually reveal how the animal once stood and moved.

choices.why: To dismantle is to take apart, the opposite of assembling bones into a complete model.
To excavate is to dig fossils out of the ground, an earlier stage than assembling the recovered bones.
To catalogue is merely to list items, not to build them into a structured whole.
'Fitting each bone into a scaffold' to form 'a complete model' defines the blank as to build by putting parts together.

stem: Few issues divide the town council so sharply; the plan to reroute the highway through the old district proved deeply ______, igniting weeks of heated hearings in which neighbors who had once agreed on everything found themselves bitterly opposed.

choices.why: 'Divide the council so sharply,' 'heated hearings,' and 'bitterly opposed' mark the plan as controversial and disputed.
Unanimous means agreed on by all, the opposite of a plan that sets neighbors bitterly against one another.
Tedious means tiresome or dull, but the hearings are described as heated, not boring.
Provisional means temporary or subject to change, which says nothing about the conflict the plan provokes.

stem: The foundation made clear that the second installment of funding was in no way guaranteed; its release would be ______ the team's demonstrated progress, disbursed only if the first year's results met the milestones both parties had agreed upon.

choices.why: 'Indifferent to' means unaffected by, but the funding depends directly on the team's progress.
'Disbursed only if the results met the milestones' shows the release is dependent or conditional on that progress.
'Prior to' marks time order, whereas the passage describes a condition, not a sequence.
'Detrimental to' means harmful to, which reverses the supportive relationship between funding and progress.

stem: Careful listeners caught the flaw at once: the witness's account contained a glaring ______, for she claimed to have been sound asleep at midnight and yet also insisted she had watched the entire argument unfold in the hallway at that very hour.

choices.why: An understatement deliberately minimizes something, but the witness's problem is two claims that cannot both be true.
A digression is a wandering aside; the flaw here is a clash between statements, not straying off topic.
Claiming to be asleep 'and yet also' to have watched the argument sets two statements in direct opposition.
A concession is an admission that grants a point, not a conflict between incompatible claims.

stem: The detective revealed that the supposed haunting was no accident of nature but the deliberate ______ a scheming heir, who had secretly rigged the creaking doors and staged the ghostly noises to frighten his relatives into fleeing the estate.

choices.why: An oversight is a careless error, but 'deliberate' and 'secretly rigged' point to intention, not accident.
A misfortune is bad luck, the opposite of a plan the heir purposely engineered.
A consequence is a mere result; the passage stresses that the haunting was purposely designed.
'Deliberate,' 'rigged the doors,' and 'staged the noises' define the haunting as a scheme or invention devised by the heir.

stem: Regulators grew suspicious when the sealed bids submitted by rival construction firms proved nearly identical: rather than competing, the companies had apparently chosen to ______, quietly coordinating their offers so that each would win a predetermined share of the public contracts.

choices.why: The clues 'quietly coordinating' and dividing contracts into a 'predetermined share' describe a secret, illicit conspiracy, which is exactly what collude means.
Collaborate means to work jointly, but it lacks the secretive, fraudulent connotation the passage stresses ('quietly,' rigged shares); open cooperation would not alarm regulators.
Compete means to strive against rivals, but the passage explicitly says the firms acted 'rather than competing.'
Negotiate means to bargain openly toward an agreement, but nothing here involves open dealing; the coordination is concealed and improper.

stem: When the youngest members of the crew returned from the failed expedition, the veteran sailors did not lecture or celebrate; instead they gathered quietly around the fire to ______ with them, sharing in the disappointment of a voyage that had cost so much and yielded so little.

choices.why: Gloat means to take smug pleasure in misfortune, but the veterans respond with fellow feeling, not triumph.
'Sharing in the disappointment' after a painful failure signals expressing sympathy together, which is what commiserate means.
Reminisce means to recall the past fondly; the sailors are sharing sorrow over a recent loss, not fondly recollecting memories.
Rejoice means to feel great joy, the opposite of the sorrow the passage describes ('cost so much and yielded so little').

stem: Throughout decades of setbacks, arrests, and public ridicule, the reformer never wavered in her campaign for voting rights; colleagues described her as utterly ______ to the cause, willing to sacrifice comfort and reputation for a goal she might not live to see achieved.

choices.why: Indifferent means showing no interest, but she sacrificed comfort and reputation for the cause.
Ambivalent means having mixed or conflicting feelings, yet the passage says she 'never wavered.'
'Never wavered' and 'willing to sacrifice comfort and reputation' point directly to being dedicated and devoted to a cause, the meaning of committed.
Obstinate means stubbornly refusing to change one's mind, implying an unreasonableness the passage does not support; it praises devotion, not intransigence.

stem: Although the two languages developed on opposite sides of the ocean and share no recent history, linguists were struck by a surprising ______: both organize their verbs according to nearly identical patterns, a resemblance that hints at deeper principles underlying human grammar.

choices.why: Disparity means a marked difference, but the passage stresses that the two languages share nearly identical patterns.
Correlation names a statistical association between varying quantities, but the passage describes a shared structural feature, not co-varying measurements.
An anomaly is a deviation from the norm, whereas the passage highlights a feature the two languages have in common.
The colon elaborates that 'both organize their verbs according to nearly identical patterns'—a shared feature, which is precisely a commonality.

stem: Only a generation ago, carrying a device that could reach the entire internet from one's pocket seemed the stuff of science fiction; today such technology is so ______ that commuters scarcely glance at the small screens glowing in every hand around them.

choices.why: 'In every hand' and 'scarcely glance' show the technology is now ordinary through sheer frequency, which is what commonplace means.
Novel means new and unusual, but the passage contrasts the once-futuristic device with its present ordinariness.
Mundane stresses dullness or tedium, whereas the passage emphasizes how widespread the technology has become, not that it is boring.
Extravagant means lavish or excessive, but the passage says nothing about cost or excess.

stem: Epidemiologists studying longevity have concentrated on the so-called Blue Zones — ______ a strikingly large share of residents older than one hundred — hoping to isolate the dietary and social habits that these long-lived populations share.

choices.why: 'Without' negates the very abundance of centenarians that defines a Blue Zone.
Blue Zones are groups defined by possessing a shared trait—a high proportion of centenarians—and 'with' marks that shared characteristic.
A single individual cannot contain a 'share of residents'; the passage describes whole groups, not persons.
'Beyond' places something past the trait rather than possessing it, describing no shared characteristic.

stem: The paleontologist's hypothesis had once been dismissed as speculation, but the discovery of fossilized nests containing both adults and hatchlings offered ______ evidence that the dinosaurs cared for their young, and even longtime skeptics found the argument difficult to refute.

choices.why: Circumstantial evidence is indirect and inconclusive, yet the passage says even skeptics could not refute it, implying strong, direct persuasion.
Tangential means only marginally relevant, but the fossils bear directly on the claim about parental care.
That the evidence convinced 'even longtime skeptics' and was 'difficult to refute' shows it was highly convincing—the meaning of compelling.
Provisional means tentative and subject to change, but the evidence is presented as decisive.

stem: When one kidney is removed, the remaining organ often grows larger and filters more blood to ______ for the loss, allowing many patients to maintain nearly normal function with a single working kidney.

choices.why: Atrophy means to waste away from disuse, but the remaining kidney enlarges and works harder.
Deteriorate means to decline in quality or function, the opposite of maintaining nearly normal function.
Substitute means to replace one thing wholesale with another, but the kidney offsets a shortfall rather than swapping in for a whole organ.
The organ 'grows larger and filters more' to make up for the missing kidney and keep function normal, which is exactly to compensate.

stem: Having dominated the market for decades, the once-innovative manufacturer let ______ set in: convinced that no rival could ever threaten its position, it stopped investing in new designs and was blindsided when nimbler competitors seized its customers.

choices.why: Being 'convinced that no rival could threaten' it and therefore ceasing to innovate is textbook complacency—smug self-satisfaction that breeds inaction.
Trepidation means nervous fear, but the firm was overconfident, not anxious.
Hubris is arrogant overpride leading to reckless overreach, whereas the passage stresses passive self-satisfaction and inaction, not prideful ambition.
Diligence is sustained careful effort, the opposite of the firm's slackening and failure to keep investing.

stem: Critics praised the film's score not because it drew attention to itself but because it was so ______ to the images on screen: the swelling strings deepened each emotional beat, and the silences let the visuals speak, so that music and picture strengthened one another.

choices.why: Extraneous means irrelevant or superfluous, but the score is integral and enhancing.
'Music and picture strengthened one another' describes two elements enhancing each other's qualities, the meaning of complementary.
Subordinate stresses being merely secondary or inferior, emphasizing hierarchy rather than the mutual enhancement the passage describes.
Identical means exactly alike, but the passage describes two different elements reinforcing each other, not sameness.

stem: The audit found that the factory's safety record had improved dramatically after new management took over, largely because of its strict ______ the international regulations governing hazardous materials, rules that earlier supervisors had routinely ignored.

choices.why: Resistance means active opposition, but the improved record came from obeying the rules, not fighting them.
Indifference is a lack of concern—precisely the attitude of the earlier supervisors who 'ignored' the rules, not the new management being credited.
'Strict' adherence to regulations, contrasted with supervisors who 'ignored' them, is exactly compliance with a standard.
Awareness means merely knowing the regulations, but the passage credits actually conforming to them for the improvement.
