stem: The region's water shortage was already severe, and a series of policy missteps only served to ______ it: subsidies encouraged farmers to plant thirsty crops, and leaking infrastructure wasted much of what little remained, deepening a crisis that sound planning might have eased.

choices.why: Alleviate means to ease or lessen, but the missteps deepened the crisis rather than relieving it.
Resolve means to settle or solve, the opposite of worsening the shortage.
Provoke means to trigger or bring something into being, but the shortage already existed; the missteps intensified it rather than initiating it.
The missteps 'only served to' worsen an already severe shortage, 'deepening a crisis'—precisely to compound a problem.

stem: The archipelago ______ more than seven thousand islands, ranging from vast, densely populated landmasses to tiny outcrops of rock that vanish beneath the waves at high tide, yet the nation governs them all under a single constitution.

choices.why: The whole (the archipelago) is made up of its parts (the seven thousand islands), the standard whole-comprises-parts relation.
Parts constitute a whole, so the islands constitute the archipelago, not the reverse; used here it inverts the part-whole relationship.
Excludes means to leave out, but the archipelago contains the islands rather than omitting them.
Resembles means to look like, but the archipelago is composed of the islands, not merely similar to them.

stem: When conservators examined the old portrait with infrared imaging, they discovered an entirely different composition ______ beneath the visible paint: the artist had abandoned an earlier scene and painted directly over it, hiding the first work for centuries.

choices.why: Displayed means openly shown, but the earlier composition was hidden under the surface layer.
'Hiding the first work for centuries' beneath the visible paint means it was kept out of sight—the meaning of concealed.
Eclipsed means overshadowed or surpassed in prominence, which concerns relative importance rather than being physically hidden from view.
Embellished means decorated or adorned, but nothing suggests the hidden scene was ornamented; it was simply painted over.

stem: For years the theorist defended his model against every objection, but as the experimental results piled up against him, he was finally forced to ______ that his rival's account explained the data more accurately than his own ever had.

choices.why: Insist means to assert firmly and persistently, but the passage shows him reluctantly giving ground under mounting evidence.
Presume means to suppose without proof, whereas he acknowledges a conclusion the accumulated evidence forced on him.
After years of resistance he was 'finally forced to' admit his rival was right—a reluctant acknowledgment, which is what concede means.
Contend means to argue or assert in a dispute, but he is yielding the dispute, not pressing his side of it.

stem: Before the first exoplanets were detected, some astronomers doubted that worlds beyond our solar system could ever be found; today, with thousands catalogued, it seems entirely ______ that at least one of them harbors the conditions necessary for life.

choices.why: Unthinkable means impossible even to imagine, the opposite of what the abundant evidence now makes easy to entertain.
Feasible means capable of being carried out, which applies to achievable actions or plans rather than to a fact being imaginable or possible.
Mandatory means required or compulsory, which concerns obligation, not possibility.
With thousands of exoplanets now found, it is easily imaginable that one supports life—exactly what conceivable means.

stem: Reviewers of the young playwright's debut praised its ambition but faulted its dialogue: at every emotional peak the characters delivered speeches that seemed engineered to manufacture feeling rather than to arise naturally from the situation, leaving even sympathetic critics convinced the drama was ______.

choices.why: The clue 'engineered to manufacture feeling rather than to arise naturally' defines something artificial and forced.
Means predictable or following a set pattern; the passage faults forced artificiality, not conventionality.
Means arising naturally and unplanned, the exact opposite of the manufactured quality described.
Means restrained or subtle; nothing concerns restraint, only over-engineered emotion.

stem: According to the colony's charter, the governor could not resolve any grievance on his own; instead, whenever a serious dispute arose among the settlers, he was obliged to ______ the general assembly so that the elected representatives could deliberate and vote together.

choices.why: Means to scatter or send away, the opposite of calling a body together.
'So that the elected representatives could deliberate and vote together' signals calling the assembly into session.
Means to bring a meeting to a close, not to summon one into being.
Means to marshal people or resources for action, not to gather a body for formal deliberation.

stem: Biologists studying unrelated species on separate continents were struck by an unexpected ______: wings had emerged independently in insects, birds, and bats, three lineages that never shared a common winged ancestor yet arrived at strikingly similar solutions to the problem of flight.

choices.why: Means a moving apart or growing difference, the opposite of the shared outcome described.
Means a breaking into separate pieces, contrary to distinct lineages arriving at the same trait.
The colon elaborates independent lineages 'arriving at strikingly similar solutions,' meeting at the same point.
Means a rapid increase in number, which the passage never mentions.

stem: Learning from the chaos of earlier disasters, the agency's new protocol required every responding group to share a single timetable and communication channel, so that in the next emergency the arrival of medical teams, food, and shelter would be tightly ______ rather than left to chance.

choices.why: Means broken into disconnected parts, the opposite of arrivals meshing on one timetable.
Means made up on the spot; that is the 'left to chance' outcome the protocol is designed to prevent.
Means made more efficient, but efficiency alone does not capture the mutual synchronization of separate groups.
Sharing 'a single timetable and communication channel' so arrivals mesh signals synchronized, jointly organized action.

stem: During her decade in the rainforest, the naturalist filled shelf after shelf with field journals; her ______ records of birdcalls, rainfall, and flowering times were so extensive that later researchers drew on them for generations.

choices.why: 'Shelf after shelf' and 'so extensive' establish an abundant, plentiful quantity.
Means scanty or insufficient, the opposite of the vast quantity described.
Means hasty and superficial, contradicting records detailed enough to serve later researchers for generations.
Means abundant but with connotations of luxury or extravagance, the wrong register for austere scientific notes.

stem: Although the two ambassadors represented empires that had warred for a generation, they greeted each other ______ at the summit, exchanging warm compliments and genuine courtesies that startled the journalists who had expected open hostility.

choices.why: Means in an abrupt, curt manner, the opposite of the warmth described.
'Warm compliments and genuine courtesies' specify a friendly, gracious manner.
Means in a proper, ceremonious way, which need not be warm or friendly and misses the affection shown.
Means in a guarded, distrustful manner, contradicting the genuine friendliness on display.

stem: The historian's bold claim rested at first on a single diary, and skeptics dismissed it; only when customs ledgers and a ship's manifest independently recorded the same voyage did her thesis gain the ______ it needed to persuade the field.

choices.why: Means evidence that disproves a claim, the opposite of the support the thesis gained.
Means conjecture without evidence, whereas the passage supplies concrete independent records.
Independent ledgers and a manifest 'recorded the same voyage,' confirming the claim with additional evidence.
Means the addition of invented or decorative detail, not the factual confirmation the thesis received.

stem: Excess carbon dioxide in the sealed greenhouse was acidifying the irrigation water, so the engineers introduced a mineral buffer designed to ______ the growing acidity and hold the water's chemistry near neutral.

choices.why: Means to make worse, the opposite of the corrective effect intended.
Means to strengthen; the buffer is meant to oppose the acidity, not intensify it.
Means to lessen severity in general, but the passage describes an opposing agent that actively neutralizes the acidity.
A buffer that opposes 'the growing acidity' to hold the chemistry 'near neutral' acts to neutralize and offset it.

stem: The fund managers built the portfolio so that its two halves moved in opposite directions: when technology holdings fell, energy holdings tended to rise, and the gains in one sector would ______ the losses in the other, keeping the total value roughly steady.

choices.why: Gains in one sector offsetting losses in another 'to keep the total value roughly steady' is the equalizing action.
Means to worsen, which would deepen the losses rather than steady the total.
Means to add to something, increasing a total rather than offsetting an opposing movement to hold it level.
Means to upset equilibrium, the opposite of the steadiness the design achieves.

stem: The result was thoroughly documented and has since been replicated many times, yet it remains ______: adding a slower lane to the congested highway actually reduced everyone's travel time, an outcome that flatly contradicts what most drivers assume must be true.

choices.why: Means obvious without proof, the opposite of a finding that defies expectation.
An outcome that 'flatly contradicts what most drivers assume' is contrary to common-sense expectation.
Implies an internal self-contradiction, but the finding is consistent and well-supported, merely surprising.
Means conforming to ordinary expectation, the opposite of what the passage describes.

stem: When trade negotiations resumed, the American finance minister spent hours on the telephone with her ______ in Tokyo, the official who held the very same portfolio in the Japanese cabinet and faced an almost identical set of pressures at home.

choices.why: Means an opponent or competitor, whereas the passage stresses an equivalent official, not an adversary.
Means a person of lower rank, but the Tokyo official holds 'the very same portfolio,' an equal position.
'The official who held the very same portfolio' in the other government is a corresponding equivalent.
Means one who previously held a post, not the person occupying the equivalent role elsewhere at the same time.

stem: Frustrated that no existing instrument could produce the sounds she imagined, the composer worked with an engineer for three years and eventually ______ an entirely new electronic keyboard, the first device of its kind ever to exist.

choices.why: Means took apart, the opposite of bringing something into being.
Means copied an existing model, whereas the passage stresses a wholly original device.
Means returned something to a former condition, but there was no prior version to bring back.
'An entirely new electronic keyboard, the first device of its kind ever to exist' signals bringing something into existence.

stem: Before reviewing a single submission, the grant panel published the ______ funding: a clear list of the standards, weighted by importance, against which the scientific merit of each proposal would be judged and ranked.

choices.why: 'A clear list of the standards ... against which the scientific merit of each proposal would be judged and ranked' defines evaluative criteria.
Names conditions required to be eligible, not the graded standards used to rank comparative merit.
Names cases exempt from a rule, unrelated to the standards of evaluation described.
Names substitutes or other options, not the measures used to judge proposals.

stem: Though the essayist admired the novel's ambition, she did not hesitate to ______ it, devoting three full pages to the wooden dialogue, the implausible ending, and the many faults she believed the author had failed to correct.

choices.why: Means to praise, the opposite of pointing out faults.
'Devoting three full pages to ... faults' expresses disapproval and identifies shortcomings.
Means to examine in detail without necessarily passing negative judgment, but the passage is explicitly fault-finding.
Means to give approval or support, contrary to the disapproval expressed.

stem: The tribunal's task was not to measure damages but to assign responsibility: after months of testimony about falsified safety reports, the judges had to determine the firm's ______ for a collapse that its own executives had knowingly risked.

choices.why: Means freedom from blame, the opposite of the responsibility the judges must assign.
Means exemption from penalty or legal consequence, not a measure of blameworthiness.
Assigning 'responsibility' for a disaster executives 'knowingly risked' is a determination of guilt or blame.
Means fault arising from carelessness, but the passage describes deliberate, knowing risk, a broader blameworthiness than mere inattention.

stem: Facing a sharp drop in tax revenue, the city council voted to ______ its after-school programs, trimming their hours and shrinking their budgets, though members insisted the services would be scaled back only temporarily rather than ended for good.

choices.why: Means to enlarge, the opposite of the reduction described.
Means to extend in duration, whereas the council is cutting hours, not lengthening them.
Means to eliminate entirely, but the passage says the programs are only scaled back, 'rather than ended for good.'
'Trimming their hours and shrinking their budgets' and being scaled back signal reducing or cutting back.

stem: Historians studying the early medieval economy face a persistent obstacle: a ______ of written records from the period, since so few documents survived that scholars must reconstruct daily life largely from scattered archaeological fragments.

choices.why: The clue 'so few documents survived' establishes an absence, so the blank must name a shortage.
Reversed: a surfeit is an excessive supply, the opposite of the scarcity the passage describes.
Unsupported: a repository is a storehouse of items, implying records exist rather than are missing.
Unsupported: a compendium is a concise collection, which again implies abundance, not lack.

stem: The anglerfish's glowing lure is remarkably ______: what appears to a small fish to be an easy meal is in fact bait dangling in front of a hidden predator that waits patiently to strike.

choices.why: Too broad: conspicuous merely means highly visible and misses the passage's emphasis on a false impression.
'What appears... is in fact bait' signals a false impression, exactly what deceptive names.
True but irrelevant: luminous describes the lure's glow but not the trickery the sentence stresses.
Unsupported: ephemeral means short-lived, and nothing in the passage concerns duration.

stem: The Battle of Yorktown proved ______ in the American Revolution: the British surrender there effectively ended major fighting and settled the war's outcome in favor of the colonists, leaving little doubt about the final result.

choices.why: Reversed: protracted means drawn out, contradicting a surrender that quickly ended the fighting.
Unsupported: ceremonial means merely formal, ignoring that the battle actually settled the war.
'Effectively ended major fighting and settled the war's outcome' defines a conclusive, outcome-determining event.
Unsupported: contentious means provoking dispute, which the passage never suggests about the battle.

stem: Emergency responders are trained to act with ______: hesitation during a crisis can cost lives, so leaders must commit to a clear course of action and issue firm orders without delay.

choices.why: Unsupported: candor is frankness or honesty, unrelated to acting quickly under pressure.
True but irrelevant: empathy may help responders but is not the quality of firm, immediate action described.
Too broad: prudence stresses caution, yet the passage praises committing without delay rather than being careful.
'Commit to a clear course of action... without delay,' set against 'hesitation,' names firm resolve.

stem: Prominent critics did not hesitate to ______ the museum's decision to sell part of its collection, publicly condemning the sale as a betrayal of the institution's duty to preserve art for the public.

choices.why: 'Publicly condemning the sale as a betrayal' matches decry, to denounce openly.
Reversed: to endorse is to approve or support, the opposite of condemning the decision.
Unsupported: to overlook is to fail to notice, but the critics clearly noticed and reacted.
Too broad: to appraise is to assess neutrally, lacking the condemnation the passage requires.

stem: In her closing essay, the scholar ______ the controversial novel against its detractors, arguing point by point that the criticisms leveled at its fractured structure misread the author's deliberate intentions.

choices.why: Reversed: to abandon is to give up on, contradicting arguing on the novel's behalf.
'Against its detractors, arguing... the criticisms misread' shows the scholar is protecting the novel.
Unsupported: to summarize is merely to condense, not to protect against attack.
Reversed: to concede is to admit the critics are right, the opposite of countering them.

stem: Although the junior architect had strong opinions about the design, she ______ the senior partner's judgment on structural matters, trusting his decades of experience over her own untested instincts.

choices.why: Reversed: to depart from a judgment is to go against it, contradicting her trust in his experience.
Unsupported: to preside over is to be in charge, illogical for a junior yielding to a senior.
'Trusting his decades of experience over her own instincts' shows she yielded to his authority.
Unsupported: to elaborate on is to add detail, not to submit to another's judgment.

stem: Analysis of the overworked farmland showed that its soil was ______ in nitrogen: crops planted there grew stunted and pale because the essential nutrient was present in far too small a quantity to sustain healthy growth.

choices.why: Reversed: saturated means fully soaked or loaded with, the opposite of a nutrient in short supply.
Reversed: abundant means plentiful, contradicting 'far too small a quantity.'
Unsupported: uniform means evenly consistent, unrelated to how much nitrogen is present.
'Present in far too small a quantity to sustain growth' defines a lacking, insufficient supply.

stem: The gyroscope's behavior seems to ______ common intuition: rather than toppling over as one expects, the rapidly spinning wheel resists the pull of gravity and remains stubbornly upright on its narrow pivot.

choices.why: 'Resists the pull of gravity... rather than toppling as one expects' matches defy, to resist or challenge.
Reversed: to confirm intuition is to bear it out, opposite of the wheel behaving unexpectedly.
Unsupported: to illustrate intuition would be to demonstrate it, but the gyroscope contradicts expectation.
Unsupported: to exceed means to surpass a limit, the wrong relationship to 'intuition.'

stem: The novelist's fragmented chronology is no accident but a ______ choice: she scrambles the timeline on purpose, forcing readers to piece events together and thereby mirroring her narrator's faulty memory.

choices.why: Reversed: haphazard means random or careless, contradicting 'no accident.'
'No accident... on purpose' signals an intentional, calculated choice.
Unsupported: conventional means ordinary or traditional, but a scrambled timeline is unusual.
Unsupported: reluctant means unwilling, which the confident, purposeful author is not.

stem: The treaty's surveyors were sent to ______ the new border, driving stone markers into the ground at regular intervals so that each nation would know precisely where its territory began and ended.

choices.why: Unsupported: to traverse is to travel across, not to mark where a territory begins and ends.
Unsupported: to populate is to fill with inhabitants, unrelated to setting boundary markers.
'Driving markers... where its territory began and ended' matches demarcate, to mark boundaries.
Reversed: to contest is to dispute, but the treaty settled rather than disputed the border.

stem: On the geologist's map, different colors ______ distinct rock types: a band of deep blue, for instance, stands for limestone, while red marks the regions built from volcanic basalt.

choices.why: Reversed: to obscure is to hide or make unclear, opposite of colors that stand for rock types.
Unsupported: to generate is to produce, but map colors represent rock rather than create it.
Unsupported: to exaggerate is to overstate, unrelated to symbolic representation.
'Stands for limestone... marks regions of basalt' matches denote, to indicate or represent.

stem: The gallery praised the young painter's ______ of rural poverty: her canvas represents the weary tenant farmers so vividly that viewers feel they are standing in the dusty field alongside them.

choices.why: 'Her canvas represents the tenant farmers so vividly' matches depiction, a representation or showing.
Reversed: concealment is hiding, opposite of a vivid public representation.
Unsupported: a critique is an evaluation, not the pictorial representation the passage praises.
Unsupported: acquisition is the act of obtaining, unrelated to how the subject is portrayed.

stem: After decades of intensive mining, the region's once-rich copper reserves were nearly ______: so much ore had been extracted that only trace amounts remained, and the exhausted pits were finally abandoned.

choices.why: Reversed: replenished means refilled or restored, contradicting 'only trace amounts remained.'
'So much ore had been extracted that only trace amounts remained' defines being used up.
Unsupported: contaminated means polluted, but the passage concerns quantity, not purity.
Unsupported: surveyed means examined or mapped, unrelated to reserves running out.

stem: Many modern medicines are ______ natural sources: aspirin, for example, traces its origins to a compound first obtained from the bark of the willow tree, which healers had used for centuries.

choices.why: Unsupported: to be immune to something is to be unaffected by it, not to originate in it.
Unsupported: to be opposed to is to be against, illogical for medicines and their sources.
'Traces its origins to a compound first obtained from' matches derived from, originating in a source.
Unsupported: identical to asserts sameness, not origin, and a medicine is not the same as its source.

stem: In her field journals, the naturalist carefully ______ each unfamiliar species she encountered, setting down in precise prose the color, size, and behavior of animals that no European had recorded before.

choices.why: Reversed: concealed means hid, opposite of setting the details down in prose.
Unsupported: domesticated means tamed, unrelated to recording species in writing.
Reversed: ignored means disregarded, contradicting careful recording.
'Setting down in precise prose the color, size, and behavior' matches described, giving a verbal account.

stem: After years of debate, the zoning board finally voted to ______ the abandoned textile mill a protected historic site, a status that legally shields the century-old building from demolition and obligates any owner to preserve its original facade.

choices.why: The board formally confers an official status ('a protected historic site'), which is exactly what it means to designate something.
To put something forward as a candidate for selection; but the board grants the status outright rather than merely proposing it for later approval.
To assess the monetary value of something, which is unrelated to conferring a protective legal status.
To tear a structure down—the direct opposite of an action that 'shields the building from demolition.'

stem: For decades the small nocturnal primate was lumped together with its larger relatives, but once genetic analysis exposed deep evolutionary differences, taxonomists granted the animal its own ______ as a distinct species.

choices.why: A line of descent or ancestry; it describes where an organism comes from, not the formal category that is 'granted' to it.
The phrase 'its own ___ as a distinct species' calls for a formal classification or title, which is precisely a designation.
The environment in which an organism lives, which has nothing to do with assigning a taxonomic category.
An animal's characteristic disposition or mood; the passage concerns classification, not behavior.

stem: Unlike scholars who pursue a single question for years, the young essayist read in a thoroughly ______ manner, drifting from botany to medieval warfare to naval history with no plan whatsoever connecting one book to the next.

choices.why: Orderly and systematic—the opposite of the planless drifting the passage describes.
Unwilling or hesitant; nothing suggests the essayist resists reading, only that his reading lacks direction.
'Drifting... with no plan whatsoever connecting one book to the next' signals reading that is aimless and random.
Unhurried and relaxed; it describes pace, but the passage stresses the absence of a guiding plan, not slowness.

stem: A skilled documentary filmmaker must balance compassion with ______: however moving her subjects' stories may be, she cannot allow personal feeling to distort her clear-eyed presentation of the facts.

choices.why: Emotional feeling—the very thing she must guard against, so it points in the wrong direction.
A pressing need for haste; the passage concerns objectivity, not time pressure.
A total lack of concern; but she still feels compassion, so this word overshoots to not caring at all.
The contrast with 'compassion' and the need to keep 'personal feeling' from distorting the facts calls for objective distance.

stem: Farmers in the arid region long relied on the plant's bitter, foul-tasting sap as a natural ______, since grazing animals quickly learned to avoid the crop and left the ripening fields entirely untouched.

choices.why: Something animals 'learned to avoid' so they leave the fields alone is exactly a discouragement or obstacle to their grazing.
Something that encourages an action; this reverses the sense, since the sap discourages rather than invites grazing.
A substance added to enrich soil; the sap repels animals rather than nourishing plants.
A physical obstruction; the sap works by taste, discouraging animals rather than physically blocking their access.

stem: Over many successive generations the isolated island finches gradually ______ beaks of markedly different shapes, each one suited to the particular seeds, insects, and fruits available in its own corner of the archipelago.

choices.why: Gave up or discarded; the finches gained specialized beaks over time rather than losing them.
'Over many successive generations' and 'gradually... markedly different shapes' signal traits that progressed and advanced over time.
Received unchanged from ancestors; but the passage stresses gradual change across generations, not a static trait passed down intact.
Hid from view; nothing suggests the beaks were hidden, only that their shapes changed.

stem: Public-health researchers set out to measure how quickly rumors ______ through a densely populated city, tracking the way a single overheard remark could reach many thousands of residents within a matter of hours.

choices.why: To become more concentrated or compact—the opposite of moving outward through a population.
To remain in one place; this contradicts the passage's emphasis on the rumor's movement across the city.
A single remark 'reaching many thousands of residents' means it spreads widely over a large area and population.
To burst out suddenly; it captures intensity but not the gradual spread of a rumor across a large group.

stem: Historians of technology often trace the ______ of the printing press across early modern Europe, mapping how the invention traveled from one commercial hub to the next until working presses operated in nearly every major town.

choices.why: A deliberate holding back or stifling—the opposite of the invention's outward movement described here.
The original act of creating the press; but the passage tracks how it later spread, not how it was first made.
The act of returning something to an earlier condition, which has no bearing on a new technology's spread.
The press 'traveled from one hub to the next until... every major town' describes its spread and distribution across a region.

stem: As the glacier retreated higher up the valley year after year, the volume of meltwater feeding the region's main river began to ______, leaving the farmers downstream with a steadily shrinking supply for their thirsty fields.

choices.why: 'A steadily shrinking supply' makes clear the volume of water becomes less and less over time.
To increase suddenly and powerfully—the reverse of the shrinking supply the passage describes.
To stop flowing or grow stale; but the passage describes a decrease in quantity, not a loss of movement.
To follow a winding course; it describes a river's path rather than its dwindling volume.

stem: The reviewer praised the novel's unflinching honesty even while conceding that its narrator is thoroughly ______: petty, rude, and quick to hurl insults at anyone who dares offer him the slightest kindness.

choices.why: Charming and magnetically likable—the opposite of the petty rudeness the list of traits describes.
'Petty, rude, and quick to hurl insults' spells out a personality that is unpleasant and unlikable.
Quiet and restrained; the narrator is loud and insulting, not withdrawn.
Unconventional or odd; oddness alone does not capture the hostility the passage details.

stem: Through the modest backyard telescope the distant galaxy appeared only as a faint gray smudge, its delicate spiral arms barely ______ against the dark sky even on the clearest and most favorable viewing nights.

choices.why: Highly visible and obvious—the opposite of arms that are only 'barely' seen.
Enormous in size; this describes magnitude, not whether something can be perceived.
A 'faint gray smudge' whose arms are 'barely ___ against the dark sky' means they can only just be perceived.
Able to be quantified; but the passage is about whether the arms can be seen at all, not measured.

stem: Only a truly ______ listener would notice that the orchestra had quietly transposed the passage upward by a single half step; to nearly everyone else in the hall, the performance sounded identical to the familiar recording.

choices.why: Inattentive and unfocused—the opposite of the sharp attention needed to catch so subtle a change.
Inexperienced and untrained; this reverses the sense, since detecting the shift requires refined perception.
Holding strong views; having opinions is unrelated to the acute perception the passage requires.
Catching a subtlety that 'nearly everyone else' misses signals a keenly perceptive, discriminating listener.

stem: The city sharply raised the tolls on its central bridge specifically to ______ downtown driving, hoping that the added expense would nudge more weekday commuters onto the newly expanded subway line instead.

choices.why: Making driving more costly so commuters shift to the subway is meant to reduce or dissuade that behavior.
To actively encourage; this reverses the intent, since the city wants less downtown driving, not more.
To make a process more efficient; a toll does not smooth out driving, and nothing supports this sense.
To ban by law; but a toll raises the cost of driving rather than prohibiting it outright.

stem: While clearing out a long-neglected storeroom in the museum's basement, a graduate student ______ a bundle of correspondence that scholars had assumed was destroyed during the war, opening an entirely new line of research.

choices.why: To lose track of something—the opposite of coming upon letters that had been assumed lost.
Coming upon a long-lost bundle 'assumed destroyed' means the student found and uncovered it for the first time.
To create a counterfeit; nothing suggests the letters are fakes rather than genuine finds.
To receive through a bequest; but she chanced upon the letters while cleaning, not by inheritance.

stem: When the auditor set the company's two ledgers side by side, she immediately flagged a troubling ______: the sum recorded as deposited each month never once matched the total the bank claimed to have received.

choices.why: General agreement—the opposite of figures that 'never once matched.'
An excess quantity; but the problem is that the numbers conflict, not that there is extra money.
Two totals that 'never once matched' are exactly an inconsistency or difference between the records.
A mutual relationship in which figures move together; the passage stresses that the numbers fail to align.

stem: Therapists often advise that in the heat of an argument it is far wiser to briefly ______ from the conversation—stepping away to cool down—than to keep pressing a point that only inflames the other person's anger.

choices.why: To gain advantage from something; nothing in the passage concerns benefit, only stepping back.
To spring back in fear or disgust; but the advice describes a calm, deliberate pause, not a startled reaction.
To refrain from something on principle; the point is a temporary withdrawal, not principled avoidance.
'Stepping away to cool down' rather than pressing on is exactly withdrawing or detaching oneself from the interaction.

stem: After the corporation repeatedly concealed the environmental damage caused by its factories, residents of the surrounding towns came to regard every subsequent press release with deep ______, assuming that each new assurance merely masked further deception.

choices.why: The clue that residents assume every assurance 'masked further deception' signals suspicion of the company's honesty, the exact meaning of distrust.
Reverence means deep respect or awe, the opposite of the wary suspicion the betrayed residents feel.
Curiosity is a desire to learn or know more; the passage describes suspicion of deceit, not interest.
Resentment names bitterness or anger at unfair treatment; it is tempting after a betrayal but does not capture the specific idea of doubting the truth of the assurances.

stem: For the first several chapters the two biographers present nearly identical accounts of the composer's childhood, but their narratives ______ sharply once they reach the disputed question of who financed his early studies.

choices.why: Converge means to come together toward a single point, the opposite of the splitting the contrast 'but... sharply' demands.
The shift from 'nearly identical accounts' to disagreement over a 'disputed question' shows the narratives branch apart, which is what diverge means.
Digress means to wander off the main topic; it describes a single speaker straying, not two accounts differing from each other.
Coincide means to agree or occur together, which contradicts the passage's move from agreement to sharp disagreement.

stem: A single hectare of tropical rainforest can shelter a strikingly ______ community of organisms, containing more species of trees, insects, and birds than are found across the whole of some temperate nations.

choices.why: Uniform means unvarying and all alike, the opposite of a community holding many different species.
Fragile means easily damaged; rainforests are indeed fragile, but the blank is defined by variety of species, not delicacy.
The clue 'more species of trees, insects, and birds' emphasizes variety of kinds, precisely what diverse means.
Abundant means present in great quantity; it is tempting but describes sheer number, whereas the clue stresses the range of different species.

stem: Although the novel tackles grave questions about mortality, its playful footnotes and comic digressions make the reading experience unexpectedly ______, prompting far more chuckles than its somber subject would seem to allow.

choices.why: Tedious means tiresome and boring, the reverse of an experience that prompts chuckles.
Engrossing means deeply absorbing; the passage points to amusement and laughter, not intense absorption.
Solemn means grave and serious, which contradicts the playful, comic tone described.
The clues 'playful,' 'comic,' and 'more chuckles' establish that the reading is amusing and entertaining, the meaning of diverting.

stem: The proposed rezoning ordinance proved deeply ______: neighbors who had cooperated for years suddenly split into rival factions, each convinced the other was betraying the community's future.

choices.why: The colon's elaboration, that neighbors 'split into rival factions,' defines the blank as something that drives people into opposing groups, which is what divisive means.
Unifying means bringing people together, the opposite of splitting a community into factions.
Provocative means tending to stir up strong feeling; it is tempting but describes arousing reaction generally, not the specific splitting into opposing sides.
Conciliatory means intended to reconcile or appease, which contradicts a measure that turns neighbors into rivals.

stem: The philosophy seminar prized open debate, so students grew frustrated with one classmate whose ______ pronouncements admitted no possibility of error and dismissed every counterargument before it could even be voiced.

choices.why: Tentative means hesitant and uncertain, the opposite of statements that admit no possibility of error.
The details that the pronouncements 'admitted no possibility of error' and dismissed all counterarguments describe stubborn, closed-minded assertion, the meaning of dogmatic.
Assertive means confident and forceful in expressing views; it is tempting but lacks the arrogant refusal to consider other perspectives that the passage stresses.
Impartial means unbiased and open to all sides, contradicting a classmate who rejects every counterargument.

stem: Buried beneath the frozen soil, the seeds can remain ______ for decades, their metabolism nearly halted, until a rare thaw finally sends the signal that prompts them to sprout.

choices.why: Flourishing means actively thriving and growing, the reverse of seeds whose metabolism is 'nearly halted.'
Volatile means unstable or liable to sudden change; nothing in the passage suggests instability, only suspended inactivity.
The phrase 'metabolism nearly halted... until a thaw prompts them to sprout' describes a temporarily inactive state that later resumes, which is exactly dormant.
Extinct means permanently died out; it is tempting for inactivity but the seeds later sprout, so their state is only temporary, not final.

stem: When the young astronomer first announced that the faint smudge was an entire galaxy beyond our own, her senior colleagues openly ______ the claim, insisting that such an object surely lay well within the boundaries of the Milky Way.

choices.why: Endorsed means approved or supported, the opposite of colleagues who insist her claim is mistaken.
Verified means confirmed as true, contradicting the colleagues' insistence that she was wrong.
Resented means felt bitterness toward; it is tempting given professional rivalry, but the clue shows they challenged the truth of her claim, not begrudged her.
Because the colleagues 'insisted' the object lay elsewhere, they questioned the reliability of her claim, which is what doubted means.

stem: Before rehearsals began, the theater company hired a ______ to research the play's historical setting, trim its unwieldy script, and advise the director on which passages would resonate with a contemporary audience.

choices.why: The duties of researching the setting, editing the script, and advising the director on staging define a dramaturge, the theatrical expert on a play's text and production.
A playwright is the author who writes an original play; the passage describes editing and advising on an existing script for a production, not composing it.
An understudy is an actor prepared to substitute for another in performance, not a specialist who researches and revises the script.
A patron is a financial backer of the arts; nothing in the passage concerns funding rather than script expertise.

stem: Each season the glacier's ______ ice reserves supplied less meltwater to the valley below, forcing farmers to abandon the very fields their families had irrigated for generations.

choices.why: Swelling means growing larger, the opposite of reserves that supply steadily less water.
The reserves 'supplied less meltwater' each season until farmers had to abandon their fields, showing a steady decrease, which is what dwindling means.
Stagnating means ceasing to develop while staying the same; the passage describes an ongoing decline, not a static level.
Fluctuating means rising and falling irregularly; it is tempting but the passage shows a consistent downward trend, not variation.

stem: As the expedition dragged into its third fruitless month, the crew felt their initial excitement steadily ______, replaced by a weary indifference to whether they ever reached the summit at all.

choices.why: Surge means to rise suddenly and powerfully, the reverse of enthusiasm giving way to weary indifference.
Intensify means to grow stronger, contradicting excitement that is 'replaced by' indifference.
The excitement is 'steadily... replaced by a weary indifference,' signaling a gradual fading, which is exactly what ebb means.
Waver means to fluctuate or hesitate; it is tempting but implies wobbling back and forth rather than the steady decline the passage describes.

stem: Neighbors traded stories about the old inventor's ______ habits: he kept every clock in his house set to a time zone of his own devising and delivered nightly lectures to the pigeons that gathered on his windowsill.

choices.why: Conventional means ordinary and conforming to custom, the opposite of the strange behavior the passage catalogs.
Meticulous means extremely careful and precise; it does not capture the oddness of inventing a private time zone or lecturing pigeons.
Reclusive means avoiding the company of others; the passage shows peculiar habits rather than a withdrawal from society.
The examples of a self-invented time zone and lectures to pigeons illustrate unconventional, peculiar behavior, which is what eccentric means.

stem: By presenting infants with brightly colored puppets, the researchers hoped to ______ a measurable response, such as a turn of the head or a widening of the eyes, that would reveal what the babies were able to perceive.

choices.why: The researchers use puppets in order to draw out an observable reaction from the infants, which is precisely what elicit means.
Suppress means to hold back or stifle; the researchers want to bring a response out, not prevent one.
Fabricate means to invent or falsify; the scientists seek a genuine reaction that reveals perception, not a manufactured one.
Anticipate means to expect in advance; it is tempting but describes predicting a response rather than drawing one out.

stem: Skilled oral historians excel at ______ candid memories from reluctant interviewees, gently phrasing each question so that even painful recollections rise to the surface without the speaker ever feeling interrogated.

choices.why: Suppressing means holding back or stifling, the opposite of drawing memories to the surface.
The historians phrase questions so that memories 'rise to the surface,' meaning they draw out those recollections, which is what eliciting means.
Cataloguing means systematically listing already-gathered material; the passage concerns coaxing memories out, not organizing them.
Embellishing means adding invented or decorative detail; that would distort the 'candid' memories the historians want to obtain.

stem: For decades the subatomic particle proved maddeningly ______: theorists were certain it existed, yet every experiment designed to capture direct evidence of it came up empty.

choices.why: Conspicuous means highly visible and obvious, the reverse of a particle no experiment can detect.
Abundant means present in great quantity and easily found, contradicting the repeated failure to capture any evidence.
The particle exists yet 'every experiment... came up empty,' showing it is difficult to find or pin down, which is what elusive means.
Hypothetical means existing only in theory; it is tempting but the passage says theorists were 'certain it existed,' so the problem is detection, not existence.

stem: Rather than recounting the shipwreck plainly, the old sailor ______ each retelling with towering waves and monstrous beasts, until the modest squall of his youth had swelled into a full-blown epic ordeal.

choices.why: Condensed means shortened or compressed, the opposite of a story that grows more elaborate with each telling.

Exaggerated means overstated in magnitude; it is tempting but the 'retelling with towering waves and monstrous beasts' points to adding decorative invented detail, the sense captured by the correct word.
Authenticated means verified as genuine, the opposite of dressing up a modest event with invented flourishes.
The sailor adorns each retelling 'with towering waves and monstrous beasts,' adding colorful and invented detail, which is exactly what embellished means.

stem: To evade predators, the leaf-tailed gecko can flatten its body and adjust its coloring to ______ itself as a patch of dead bark, becoming so convincing that even sharp-eyed birds pass over it as they scan the tree trunk for a meal.

choices.why: The clue 'as a patch of dead bark' and 'so convincing... pass over it' shows the gecko alters its appearance to pass as something else, which is exactly what disguise means.
Reversed: advertise means to draw attention to something, the opposite of hiding from birds.
Too broad: obscure means to make dim or unclear, but the passage describes actively impersonating dead bark, not merely blurring itself.
Unsupported: dislodge means to knock something loose from a fixed position, which has nothing to do with the gecko's appearance.

stem: Boulders had sat wedged in the narrow gorge for centuries, but the sheer power of the flash flood was finally enough to ______ them, sending the massive stones tumbling downstream in a matter of seconds.

choices.why: Too broad: erode means to wear away gradually, but the flood knocked whole boulders loose in seconds, a sudden forceful removal.
The clue 'wedged... for centuries' plus 'enough to ___ them, sending the stones tumbling downstream' signals removing objects by force from a fixed position, the meaning of dislodge.
Reversed: buttress means to prop up or support in place, the opposite of forcing the boulders loose.
Unsupported: submerge means to cover with water, which says nothing about removing the wedged stones.

stem: When Alfred Wegener first proposed that the continents had once been joined and had drifted apart, many established geologists were quick to ______ his idea as idle speculation, waving it aside without seriously weighing the evidence he had gathered.

choices.why: Reversed: endorse means to support or approve, but the geologists rejected Wegener's idea.
Reversed: scrutinize means to examine closely, the opposite of waving the idea aside 'without seriously weighing the evidence.'
The clue 'as idle speculation, waving it aside without seriously weighing the evidence' shows they rejected the idea as unworthy of consideration, the meaning of dismiss.
Too specific: rebut means to refute with a counterargument, but dismiss captures brushing the idea off without engaging it at all, as the passage stresses.

stem: The abrupt ______ of the newspaper's veteran editor, announced one morning without any stated reason, stunned the entire staff; within a week, several reporters had walked out in protest of the leadership's decision to force her out.

choices.why: Reversed: promotion means an advancement in rank, but the editor was forced out, not elevated.
Reversed: commendation means formal praise, the opposite of the punitive removal the staff protested.
Too specific: resignation is a voluntary departure, but the passage says the editor was forced out by others, not that she chose to leave.
The clues 'without any stated reason' and 'force her out' point to a removal or discharge from her position, which is what dismissal means.

stem: Visitors to the mirrored gallery often describe the experience as deeply ______: the endless reflections erase any sense of where the walls actually begin, leaving even seasoned museumgoers turning in circles, unsure which way leads back to the exit.

choices.why: The clues 'erase any sense of where the walls begin' and 'unsure which way leads back' describe a loss of one's bearings, the meaning of disorienting.
Reversed: illuminating means clarifying or enlightening, the opposite of the confusion the mirrors create.
True but irrelevant: immersive means absorbing and enveloping, which the gallery may be, but it says nothing about losing one's sense of direction.
Unsupported: monotonous means tediously repetitive, but nothing suggests the experience is dull.

stem: Early reviewers were quick to ______ Emily Dickinson's unconventional style, dismissing her dashes and slanted rhymes as the careless mistakes of an untrained amateur rather than recognizing them as bold and deliberate artistic choices.

choices.why: Reversed: celebrate means to praise or honor, the opposite of calling her work careless mistakes.
The clue 'the careless mistakes of an untrained amateur' shows the reviewers were belittling Dickinson's style, which is what disparage means.
Too broad: critique means to evaluate, which can be neutral or fair, but the passage shows the reviewers were specifically running the work down.
Unsupported: emulate means to imitate admiringly, but the reviewers scorned her work rather than copying it.

stem: The accuracy of modern climate models depends on weaving together strikingly ______ streams of evidence, including ice-core samples, satellite images, ocean-buoy readings, and tree-ring records, and fusing these unlike sources into one coherent simulation of the planet's past.

choices.why: Reversed: uniform means consistent and alike, but the passage lists sources that differ fundamentally in kind.
True but irrelevant: voluminous means large in quantity, which may describe the data's bulk, but the sentence stresses how unlike the sources are, not how much data there is.
The list of very different evidence types plus 'these unlike sources' signals data that is distinct and dissimilar in nature, the meaning of disparate.
Reversed: identical means exactly the same, but ice cores, satellites, buoys, and tree rings are anything but the same.

stem: A recent public-health study documented a striking ______ in life expectancy between two neighborhoods only a few miles apart: residents of the wealthier district lived, on average, a full decade longer than their neighbors in the poorer one.

choices.why: Reversed: parity means equality, but the study found a ten-year gap, not equal outcomes.
Unsupported: consensus means general agreement, which has nothing to do with a difference in life expectancy.
Too broad: variation means ordinary range of difference, but disparity better captures the stark, consequential ten-year gap the passage emphasizes.
The clue 'a full decade longer' between two nearby neighborhoods signals a marked difference or gap, which is what disparity means.

stem: By the time the autumn gusts died down, the dandelion's tiny seeds had been ______ across the entire meadow, carried so far on the wind that scarcely any of them settled anywhere near the plant that had produced them.

choices.why: The clues 'across the entire meadow' and 'carried so far... scarcely any settled near the plant' describe seeds scattered widely, which is what dispersed means.
Reversed: concentrated means gathered densely in one place, the opposite of seeds flung across the whole meadow.
Too specific: deposited means set down in a particular spot, but the passage stresses wide scattering, not settling in one location.
Wrong domain: cultivated means deliberately grown or tended, but wind-blown seeds were spread by chance, not cultivated.

stem: Even after Galileo published his observations, several astronomers continued to ______ his claim that Jupiter had moons, arguing forcefully that the specks he had recorded were nothing more than flaws in the glass of his primitive telescope.

choices.why: Reversed: corroborate means to confirm or support with evidence, but these astronomers were arguing against Galileo's claim.
The clue 'arguing forcefully that the specks were nothing more than flaws' shows the astronomers were challenging and contesting the claim, which is what dispute means.
Too broad: dismiss means to reject outright without engaging, but the passage shows the astronomers actively arguing a counterexplanation, which is disputing.
Reversed: concede means to admit or accept as true, the opposite of resisting Galileo's claim.

stem: Confident in their own maps, the expedition's leaders chose to ______ the repeated warnings of local guides about the mountain's sudden afternoon storms, a decision that stranded the party above the tree line and nearly cost every member their life.

choices.why: Reversed: heed means to pay careful attention and act on advice, but the leaders ignored the guides and paid dearly.
Unsupported: exaggerate means to overstate, but the leaders took the warnings less seriously, not more.
The clue 'confident in their own maps' plus the disastrous outcome shows the leaders ignored the guides' warnings, which is what disregard means.
Too specific: downplay means to make something seem less important, but the passage shows the leaders ignored the warnings entirely rather than merely minimizing them.

stem: As the final encore faded, the electric tension that had gripped the packed arena began to ______; within minutes the once-frenzied crowd had settled into calm, unhurried streams filing quietly toward the exits.

choices.why: Reversed: intensify means to grow stronger, but the tension was fading as the crowd grew calm.
Reversed: linger means to persist and remain, the opposite of tension melting away within minutes.
Unsupported: resurface means to reappear after being hidden, but the tension was disappearing, not returning.
The clue 'within minutes the once-frenzied crowd had settled into calm' shows the tension scattered and faded away, which is what dissipate means.

stem: Alarmed that her findings were being cited to justify the sweeping policy, the biologist publicly moved to ______ herself from the campaign entirely, insisting that her data had been twisted beyond recognition and demanding that her name be removed from its literature.

choices.why: The clues 'insisting her data had been twisted' and 'demanding her name be removed' show she is severing her connection to the campaign, which is what dissociate means.
Reversed: align means to join with or take the side of, the opposite of the biologist distancing herself.
Unsupported: reconcile means to restore friendly relations, but she is cutting ties, not repairing them.
Reversed: implicate means to show involvement in, connecting her to the campaign rather than separating her from it.

stem: After months of legislative gridlock had paralyzed the government, the king ordered the ______ of parliament, formally sending every representative home, terminating the body entirely, and calling for fresh elections to be held the following spring.

choices.why: Unsupported: ratification means formal approval of an agreement, but the passage describes ending a body, not approving one.
The clues 'sending every representative home, terminating the body entirely' and calling fresh elections describe the formal ending of an official assembly, which is what dissolution means.
Too specific: adjournment is a temporary suspension of a session, but the king permanently terminated parliament and called new elections.
Reversed: convening means assembling a body together, the opposite of disbanding it.

stem: Over thousands of years, mildly acidic rainwater seeps into the ground and can chemically ______ solid limestone, breaking the rock apart at the molecular level and washing the minerals away to hollow out the vast chambers and winding passages of a cave system.

choices.why: Reversed: fortify means to strengthen or reinforce, but the rainwater is breaking the rock down, not building it up.
Too broad: erode means to wear away gradually by mechanical action, but the passage specifies a chemical breakdown 'at the molecular level,' which is dissolving.
The clue 'chemically... breaking the rock apart at the molecular level and washing the minerals away' describes matter breaking down into a liquid, which is what dissolve means.
Reversed: petrify means to harden into stone, the opposite of breaking the limestone down.

stem: The nurse handed the child a brightly colored puzzle and used it as a ______ the frightened toddler, drawing her attention entirely to the shapes and colors so that the doctor could administer the vaccine before she even noticed the needle.

choices.why: Unsupported: a reward is given in recognition of behavior, but the puzzle's purpose was to divert the child's attention, not to reward her.
True but irrelevant: comfort means solace, tempting because the child is frightened, but the passage stresses drawing her attention away, not soothing her feelings.
Reversed: a deterrent discourages an action, the opposite of engaging the toddler's attention with the puzzle.
The clue 'drawing her attention entirely to the shapes... so the doctor could administer the vaccine before she noticed' shows something used to divert her focus, which is a distraction for her.

stem: Because the archive's fifteenth-century manuscripts demand highly specialized handling, the university's librarians voted to ______ their conservation to a private laboratory whose staff has spent decades stabilizing fragile parchment.

choices.why: To attribute is to credit something as a cause or source; the librarians are assigning a duty, not assigning credit for one.
To relegate is to consign to an inferior position or rank; the passage presents the laboratory as a respected expert, not a lesser destination.
The manuscripts 'demand highly specialized handling' and the lab has 'decades' of expertise, so the librarians are confidently assigning the care to a trusted party — precisely what entrust means.
To abandon something to someone is to give it up carelessly or in defeat; the vote described is a deliberate, trusting delegation, not a careless surrender.

stem: Environmental artist Andy Goldsworthy builds his sculptures from ice, leaves, and blown petals precisely because such works are ______: most dissolve, scatter, or melt within hours of completion, surviving only in photographs.

choices.why: The colon introduces the elaboration 'dissolve, scatter, or melt within hours,' so the blank must mean lasting a very short time.
Enduring means lasting a long time — the direct opposite of works that vanish within hours.
Sporadic means occurring irregularly or infrequently; the passage concerns how long the works last, not how often they appear.
Monumental describes something massive and built to last; sculptures that melt in hours are the reverse of permanent monuments.

stem: With its rigorously symmetrical façade, harmonious proportions, and temple-front portico, Palladio's Villa Rotonda is widely regarded as the ______ of Renaissance classicism: nearly every ideal the movement articulated finds full expression in the building.

choices.why: An antithesis is a direct opposite; the villa expresses the movement's ideals rather than contradicting them.
A forerunner precedes and anticipates a movement; the villa embodies ideals the movement had already articulated, so it exemplifies rather than foreshadows them.
A vestige is a surviving trace of something that has largely vanished; nothing in the passage suggests classicism had disappeared.
The colon explains that 'nearly every ideal ... finds full expression in the building,' so the blank must mean the perfect example or embodiment.

stem: Historians argue that the Crystal Palace, erected for the Great Exhibition of 1851, came to ______ Victorian faith in industrial progress: its vast iron-and-glass frame displayed the era's confidence in engineering more completely than any other structure.

choices.why: To contradict is to assert the opposite; the building displayed the era's confidence rather than opposing it.
The colon's claim that the building displayed the era's confidence 'more completely than any other structure' means it was the perfect example of that faith — exactly what epitomize means.
To exaggerate is to overstate or distort beyond the truth; the passage says the structure faithfully expressed the era's faith, not that it inflated it.
To commemorate is to honor the memory of something past; Victorian faith in progress was a living attitude, not a bygone event being memorialized.

stem: Reviewers hailed the author's debut collection as ______ the spare aesthetic of literary minimalism, noting that each pared-down story distilled the movement's ideals of restraint and omission into their purest form.

choices.why: Repudiating means rejecting or disowning; the stories realize the movement's ideals rather than refusing them.
Embellishing means adding decorative detail — the opposite of the 'pared-down' restraint and omission the passage describes.
Each story 'distilled the movement's ideals ... into their purest form,' so the collection serves as a perfect example of the aesthetic — the meaning of epitomizing.
Anticipating implies coming before something; minimalism is an established movement with articulated ideals here, so the stories embody it rather than foreshadow it.

stem: During the congressional hearing, the executive repeatedly sought to ______ questions about the firm's accounting practices, responding with vague generalities whenever senators pressed for specific figures.

choices.why: Answering with 'vague generalities' instead of the requested specifics is a way of avoiding the questions — the core meaning of evade.
To rebut is to argue directly against a claim with counterevidence; vague generalities are dodges, not counterarguments.
To clarify is to make clearer; offering vague generalities is the opposite of clarification.
To anticipate is to foresee or prepare for in advance; the passage describes his behavior during questioning, not any advance preparation.

stem: Tiger moths respond to a bat's sonar with sudden dives and erratic spirals, a strategy of ______ that lets the insects slip free of pursuit rather than confront their predators directly.

choices.why: Retaliation means striking back; the moths flee, and the passage explicitly rules out confronting the predator.
The appositive defines the strategy as one that lets the moths 'slip free of pursuit,' which is exactly what evasion — escape or avoidance — means.
Camouflage is concealment by blending into surroundings; dives and spirals are conspicuous escape maneuvers, not disguise.
Migration is seasonal, long-distance relocation; a split-second dodge of a hunting bat is out of that word's scope entirely.

stem: Ethnographers increasingly describe cultural traditions not as static inheritances passed down intact but as ______ practices, gradually reshaped as each generation reinterprets old rituals to fit new circumstances.

choices.why: Unchanging repeats the idea of 'static inheritances passed down intact,' which the sentence's 'not ... but' structure explicitly rejects.
Vanishing means disappearing; the traditions are being transformed and carried forward, not lost.
Recurring means happening again and again; traditions do repeat, but the contrast with 'static' demands change over time, not mere repetition.
The contrast marker 'not ... but' opposes 'static,' and 'gradually reshaped as each generation reinterprets' defines gradual development over time — the meaning of evolving.

stem: Hydrologists warned that diverting the river for irrigation would ______ the region's water crisis rather than relieve it, deepening shortages downstream even as upstream fields temporarily flourished.

choices.why: The contrast 'rather than relieve it' plus 'deepening shortages' shows the diversion makes the crisis worse — exactly what exacerbate means.
Alleviate means to ease or relieve, the very outcome the sentence explicitly rules out with 'rather than relieve it.'
Prolong means only to extend something's duration; 'deepening shortages' indicates growing severity, not merely a longer timeline.
Forestall means to prevent something before it happens; the crisis already exists and the diversion intensifies it.

stem: The nineteenth-century cartographer's coastal surveys were prized for their ______: repeated triangulations fixed each headland's position to within a few meters, and later satellite imaging confirmed the measurements almost point for point.

choices.why: Ambiguity means openness to multiple interpretations; positions fixed 'to within a few meters' are the opposite of ambiguous.
Grandeur means impressive scale or splendor; the passage praises the surveys' measurements, not their magnificence.
The colon elaborates with positions fixed 'to within a few meters' and later confirmed 'point for point,' so the blank must name the quality of precision.
Thoroughness is completeness of coverage; the clue concerns how precisely each point was fixed, not whether every feature was included.

stem: Engineers report that the laboratory's new perovskite solar cells ______ the efficiency of conventional silicon panels by a wide margin, converting nearly ten percent more of the available sunlight into usable electricity.

choices.why: Match means to equal; 'by a wide margin' and 'ten percent more' describe surpassing, not parity.
'By a wide margin' and 'ten percent more' show the new cells go beyond the old panels' efficiency — the meaning of exceed.
Approach means to come near to a level while still falling short; the cells have already surpassed the panels, not merely closed the gap.
Trail means to lag behind; converting ten percent more sunlight puts the new cells ahead, not behind.

stem: Scholars of medieval art routinely treat the Book of Kells as the finest ______ of insular illumination, a model whose intricate initials and interlace set the standard against which other manuscripts are judged.

choices.why: An anomaly deviates from the norm; the manuscript defines the norm, since others are judged against it.
An imitation is a copy of something else; the appositive calls the book 'a model ... [that] set the standard' — the thing copied, not the copy.
A fragment is a broken-off or incomplete piece; nothing in the passage suggests the manuscript is partial or damaged.
The appositive 'a model ... set the standard against which other manuscripts are judged' defines an ideal example — precisely what exemplar means.

stem: Participants in the sports-psychology study consistently described their first white-water rafting run as ______, reporting surges of elation and heightened energy that persisted for hours after they left the river.

choices.why: Harrowing means acutely distressing; the participants report elation and energy, and nothing in the passage indicates distress.
'Surges of elation and heightened energy' directly restates the meaning of exhilarating — making one feel elated and animated.
Monotonous means dull and unvarying; a run that produces hours of elation is the opposite of tedious.
Soothing means calming; 'heightened energy' describes arousal and excitement, not relaxation.

stem: Letters from the California gold fields complain that merchants in remote mining camps charged ______ prices for basic supplies: a barrel of flour costing six dollars in San Francisco might sell for ten times that sum upriver.

choices.why: Negligible means too small to matter; a tenfold markup is anything but trivial.
Competitive prices are in line with or below the going market rate; ten times the San Francisco price is far above it.
The colon's example — flour selling for 'ten times' its city price — plus the miners' complaints show the prices were unreasonably excessive, the meaning of exorbitant.
Arbitrary means set by whim without reason; the passage's clue quantifies how excessively high the prices were, not how randomly they were chosen.

stem: Responding to reviewers who found her first edition's central claim underdeveloped, the historian used the new preface to ______ her original argument, supplying two additional case studies and a fuller account of her sources.

choices.why: Supplying 'additional case studies and a fuller account' answers the charge that the claim was 'underdeveloped' — she elaborates with further detail, the meaning of expand on.
To gloss over is to pass by quickly without detail; adding case studies and fuller sourcing is the opposite of skimming past.
To detract from is to diminish something's force or value; the new material strengthens and develops the argument.
To capitalize on is to exploit something for advantage; the passage describes scholarly elaboration, not opportunistic gain.

stem: Critics of the 1878 treaty argued that its terms reflected not principle but ______: the diplomats accepted whatever boundary lines could be ratified quickly, deferring every question of justice to later conferences.

choices.why: Idealism is commitment to principle over practicality — the very motive the sentence denies with 'not principle but.'
Transparency means openness about one's dealings; the passage concerns the diplomats' motives, and secrecy is never at issue.
Deliberation is slow, careful weighing of options; accepting 'whatever ... could be ratified quickly' rules out unhurried consideration.
The contrast 'not principle but' plus accepting 'whatever ... could be ratified quickly' while deferring justice defines choosing convenience over principle — the meaning of expediency.

stem: When a struggling museum finally recognized that its aging exhibits deterred younger visitors, its board voted to ______ digital installations that critics had once dismissed as gimmicks—a decision that ultimately reversed years of declining attendance.

choices.why: The board reversed declining attendance by actively taking up installations it once dismissed, so the blank must mean to accept and adopt—embrace.
Spurn means to reject with contempt, the opposite of the board's decision to welcome the new installations.
Tolerate means merely to put up with; the board did more than passively allow the installations—it committed to them.
Scrutinize means to examine closely; nothing in the passage concerns inspecting the installations, only deciding to adopt them.

stem: Comparing several surviving copies of the medieval chronicle, the scholar found that a single scribal slip had been propagated for centuries; only by consulting the earliest manuscript could she ______ the passage and restore the author's original wording.

choices.why: Transcribe means to copy out text; that is precisely what the earlier scribes did wrong—the scholar needed to correct, not merely copy.
The scholar aims to remove a propagated error and restore the original wording, so the blank must mean to correct a text—emend.
Fabricate means to invent or falsify, the opposite of restoring an author's true original wording.
Censor means to suppress objectionable content; the passage concerns fixing an error, not removing offensive material.

stem: Unable to cross the treacherous mountain passes himself, the aging monarch dispatched trusted ______ to the rival court, empowering them to negotiate a treaty and speak on his behalf.

choices.why: Mercenaries are soldiers who fight for pay; the monarch's agents were sent to negotiate, not to wage war.
Dissidents oppose the ruling authority, whereas these agents act on the monarch's behalf, not against him.
They are dispatched to the rival court, empowered to negotiate and to speak on the monarch's behalf—the defining role of emissaries.
Chroniclers record events in writing; nothing suggests the agents were historians rather than negotiators.

stem: The critic praised the novel's final paragraph for its economy: in two spare sentences it seemed to ______ the entire family's decades of quiet disappointment, distilling a sprawling saga into a single, resonant image.

choices.why: Embellish means to add decorative detail, the opposite of the economy and distillation the passage praises.
To catalog is to list items one by one; the paragraph condenses a saga into a single image rather than enumerating it.
Protract means to draw out or lengthen, contradicting the praised brevity of 'two spare sentences.'
'Distilling a sprawling saga into a single, resonant image' signals compressing an entire meaning into a tiny space—to encapsulate.

stem: As the aurora rippled in green sheets across the polar sky, the exhausted researchers forgot their frostbitten fingers entirely, watching in silent ______ as the lights folded and unfurled overhead.

choices.why: The researchers forget their pain and watch the lights in rapt silence, a scene of delight and wonder—enchantment.
Trepidation is fearful anxiety; the passage conveys pleasure, not dread.
Indifference is a lack of interest, contradicting their transfixed, absorbed watching.
Bewilderment is confusion; the researchers are captivated, not puzzled, by the aurora.

stem: Ecologists stress that a truly protected watershed must ______ not only the river itself but also the surrounding wetlands, forested slopes, and underground aquifers that feed it, since safeguarding one part while ignoring the rest accomplishes little.

choices.why: Bypass means to go around or leave out, the opposite of holding all the elements within a protected area.
The watershed must hold the river 'and also' the wetlands, slopes, and aquifers within it, so the blank means to surround and include—encompass.
Enumerate means to list one by one; the passage is about containing these features, not counting them.
Fragment means to break into pieces, contradicting the call to keep the watershed's parts protected together.

stem: Rather than penalizing students for wrong answers, the new teaching method is designed to ______ intellectual risk-taking: pupils earn recognition simply for proposing bold hypotheses, whether or not those guesses ultimately prove correct.

choices.why: Stifle means to suppress or smother; the method rewards risk-taking rather than shutting it down.
Mandate means to command by rule; the method offers recognition and support, not compulsion, and bold guessing cannot simply be ordered.
Pupils earn recognition for bold hypotheses regardless of correctness, a system built to inspire and support risk-taking—encourage.
Deter means to discourage, the opposite of fostering risk-taking.

stem: Studies of open-plan offices suggest that placing communal coffee stations at busy intersections ______ spontaneous collaboration, as employees who might never schedule a meeting end up trading ideas while waiting for the kettle.

choices.why: Permits means merely to allow; the stations actively prompt collaboration rather than just tolerating it.
Suppresses means to hold back, the opposite of fostering spontaneous exchanges of ideas.
Mimics means to imitate; nothing suggests the stations copy collaboration—they generate it.
Employees who would never schedule a meeting end up trading ideas at the stations, so the design actively fosters collaboration—encourages.

stem: Archaeologists marvel that the Roman aqueduct, assembled without mortar from precisely cut stone, could ______ two thousand years of earthquakes and floods while far newer structures nearby have already crumbled into rubble.

choices.why: The aqueduct lasted through two millennia of earthquakes and floods while newer structures crumbled, so the blank means to withstand and survive—endure.
Collapse means to fall apart, exactly what the surviving aqueduct did not do.
Predate means to come before in time; the point is survival through the centuries, not chronological precedence.
Succumb means to give way or yield, the opposite of surviving harsh forces intact.

stem: Though many bestselling novels of the 1850s were forgotten within a generation, Melville's work has proven surprisingly ______: it is still debated in classrooms and reinterpreted by artists more than a century and a half after its lukewarm initial reception.

choices.why: Fleeting means short-lived, contradicting a reputation still alive a century and a half later.
Unlike novels forgotten within a generation, Melville's work is still debated and reinterpreted long after publication, so the blank means lasting—enduring.
Immutable means incapable of change; yet the work is continually reinterpreted, so it is lasting, not unchanging.
Derivative means imitative and unoriginal; the passage concerns the work's longevity, not its originality.

stem: Economists warn that abruptly slashing food subsidies, however sound in theory, tends to ______ widespread unrest, as families who suddenly cannot afford staples take their grievances into the streets.

choices.why: Quell means to put down or suppress; slashing subsidies produces unrest rather than quieting it.
Forecast means to predict; the passage says the policy causes unrest, not that it merely anticipates it.
Families who cannot afford staples take grievances to the streets, so cutting subsidies gives rise to unrest—engender.
Alleviate means to ease; the policy worsens hardship and provokes unrest, the opposite of relieving it.

stem: The rapid spread of generative image tools is ______ fresh anxieties among photographers, who fear that a flood of synthetic pictures will make it impossible for audiences to trust that any photograph depicts a real event.

choices.why: Dispelling means driving away; the tools create new anxieties rather than removing them.
Documenting means recording; the tools generate the fears, not merely note them down.
Mirroring means reflecting something that already exists, but the passage says the fears are freshly produced.
Photographers' fear of a flood of synthetic images is an anxiety newly produced by the tools' spread, so the blank means causing—engendering.

stem: When a pyroclastic flow races down a volcano's flank, it ______ everything in its path within seconds, burying forests, roads, and entire villages beneath a searing avalanche of ash and gas.

choices.why: The flow buries forests, roads, and villages beneath ash within seconds, completely and overwhelmingly covering everything—engulfs.
Spares means to leave unharmed, the opposite of burying everything in its path.
Skirts means to pass around the edge of; the flow overruns everything rather than avoiding it.
Grazes means to touch lightly; the intensity is far too weak for an avalanche that buries entire villages.
