Integral to means an essential part of something, contradicting the anecdote's dismissal as beside the point.
Analogous to means similar or parallel, but the passage stresses disconnection, not resemblance.
'Shed no light on' the principle shows the anecdote is not connected to the matter at hand—exactly irrelevant to it.

stem: Across four decades on the bench, the judge maintained a record so ______ that even her fiercest political opponents, who scrutinized every ruling for a hint of impropriety, could never find a single fault to exploit.

choices.why: The clue that even hostile scrutineers 'could never find a single fault' points to a record that is entirely blameless—irreproachable.
Commendable means praiseworthy but still admits shortcomings; it falls short of the flawlessness the passage insists on.
Ambitious describes drive for success, which has nothing to do with being free of fault.
Questionable means doubtful or suspect, the opposite of a record no critic could fault.

stem: Before the expedition set out across the highlands, the guide handed each traveler a detailed ______ that laid out every day's destinations, the estimated hours of walking, and the villages where the group would stop to rest.

choices.why: A manifesto is a public declaration of aims or beliefs, not a day-by-day plan of a journey.
A document listing each day's destinations and stops along the route is the definition of an itinerary.
An inventory is a list of goods or supplies, not the planned course of travel described here.
A memoir is a personal account written after events, whereas this document is prepared before the trip.

stem: New employees regularly got lost in the agency's ______ approval process—a bewildering maze of forms, overlapping sign-offs, and cross-references that seemed almost deliberately designed to confuse anyone trying to navigate it.

choices.why: Streamlined means made simple and efficient, the reverse of a bewildering maze that confuses people.
Transparent means easy to understand, contradicting a process described as confusing to navigate.
'A bewildering maze' of forms and cross-references designed to confuse describes a twisting, intricate tangle—labyrinthine.
Lengthy captures only duration; it misses the maze-like, confusing complexity the passage emphasizes.

stem: The soil samples explained why the seedlings had withered: the exhausted fields were entirely ______ the nitrogen that young plants must draw from the ground in order to grow strong stems and broad, healthy leaves.

choices.why: Harboring means holding or possessing, the reverse of the deficiency that caused the seedlings to wither.
Depleting describes actively using something up, not the static absence of nitrogen the samples revealed.
Replenishing means refilling a supply, contradicting the passage's account of failed, nutrient-poor fields.
The withered seedlings and 'exhausted fields' show the soil is deficient in nitrogen—the meaning of lacking.

stem: When the young playwright's debut finally opened, the reviewers did not merely find minor faults with it—they ______ it, condemning nearly every scene in language so scathing that the production shut down within a single week.

choices.why: 'Condemning nearly every scene in language so scathing' describes harsh, severe criticism—exactly what lambasted means.
Lauded means praised highly, the reverse of scathing condemnation that closes a show.
Analyzed suggests neutral, detailed examination, not the fierce attack the passage describes.
Critiqued means reviewed or evaluated and lacks the intensity of the brutal condemnation described here.

stem: The virus can remain ______ within the body for years, producing no symptoms whatsoever, until some physical or emotional stressor finally rouses it and triggers a full-blown active infection.

choices.why: Virulent describes a severe, actively harmful state, the opposite of lying quietly without symptoms.
'Producing no symptoms' for years until something 'rouses it' describes a hidden, dormant presence—latent.
Apparent means clearly visible or manifest, contradicting a virus that produces no symptoms.
The virus may indeed be contagious, but the passage stresses its dormancy, not its transmissibility.

stem: After the bitterly disputed election, international observers spent weeks authenticating the ballots before finally declaring the new administration ______—the lawful and rightful authority to be recognized by every neighboring state.

choices.why: Provisional means temporary or interim, whereas the passage certifies a lawful, established authority.
Autonomous means self-governing or independent, which the ballot verification does not address.
'The lawful and rightful authority' after ballots were authenticated names a government that is legitimate.
Fraudulent means obtained by deceit, the reverse of an administration certified as lawful.

stem: At first the outbreak was ______, affecting only a handful of villages clustered in one narrow river valley; it was not until travelers unknowingly carried the illness overseas that it swelled into a global concern.

choices.why: Chronic describes something long-lasting in time, but the passage contrasts area, not duration.
Airborne names a mode of transmission, which the passage never mentions.
Rampant means spreading unchecked everywhere, the reverse of an outbreak confined to a few villages.
'Affecting only a handful of villages in one narrow valley' shows the outbreak was confined to a specific area—localized.

stem: After her children moved abroad and her closest friends passed away, the widow described in the novel spends her evenings staring at the phone that never rings; the author renders her as profoundly ______, aching for the companionship that once filled her home.

choices.why: The clue 'aching for the companionship that once filled her home' pins the blank to the feeling of isolation and lack of company.
Solitary merely means being alone, often by choice; it misses the emotional deprivation the passage stresses with 'aching for companionship.'
Secluded describes a place that is hidden or private, not a person's yearning for company; wrong domain.
Indifferent means emotionally detached or uncaring, the opposite of a woman aching for connection.

stem: The spice trade of the fifteenth century proved so ______ that European monarchs financed perilous ocean voyages in pursuit of it: a single successful shipment of nutmeg or cloves could yield profits many times the cost of the expedition.

choices.why: Advantageous means generally beneficial but does not specifically denote producing income; the clue is about 'profits many times the cost.'
The elaboration 'could yield profits many times the cost' names financial profitability, which is exactly what lucrative means.
Exorbitant describes a price that is excessively high, not the profitability of a venture; wrong dimension.
Prohibitive means so costly as to prevent an action, which would discourage rather than fund the voyages.

stem: Researchers studying infant development note that certain temperamental traits ______ themselves very early: babies as young as four months will visibly display the wariness or exuberance that comes to define their later personalities.

choices.why: Disguise means to hide or mask, the opposite of the visible display the colon describes.
Anticipate means to expect in advance; the passage is about traits being outwardly shown, not predicted.
The colon's elaboration 'will visibly display the wariness or exuberance' matches manifest, to show a quality by one's acts or appearance.
Induce means to bring about or cause; the passage describes traits appearing, not being triggered into existence.

stem: Sociologists argue that fashion trends are rarely superficial; a sudden collective embrace of austere, minimal clothing, for instance, can be read as a visible ______ of deeper economic anxiety, an outward expression of feelings the public rarely states aloud.

choices.why: A catalyst is a cause that triggers something; here the anxiety causes the trend, so the direction is reversed.
An anomaly is an irregularity or deviation; nothing marks the trend as abnormal.
An epitome is the perfect embodiment of a type; that overstates and misses the passage's focus on outward expression.
The appositive 'an outward expression of feelings the public rarely states aloud' defines the blank precisely as a manifestation.

stem: By the time she was twenty, the young cellist had achieved such complete ______ the instrument that even the most technically demanding passages seemed effortless under her fingers.

choices.why: The result clause 'even the most technically demanding passages seemed effortless' signals command and proficiency, exactly mastery over.
Aversion to means a strong dislike, which would not produce effortless, expert playing.
Exposure to means mere contact or familiarity, which falls short of the command the effortlessness implies.
Reliance on means dependence; being dependent on the instrument says nothing about skill in playing it.

stem: The historian argued that the newly discovered letters were ______ any honest account of the treaty negotiations: without them, scholars had been overlooking the private doubts that shaped the final agreement.

choices.why: Peripheral to means of marginal importance, the opposite of the significance the clue 'shaped the final agreement' establishes.
'Without them, scholars had been overlooking the private doubts that shaped the agreement' shows the letters are relevant and significant, i.e., material to the account.
Consistent with means in agreement with; the passage stresses importance, not whether the letters agree with the account.
Analogous to means similar or comparable to, which is the wrong kind of relation between the letters and the account.

stem: Stranded by the early blizzard, the expedition survived for weeks on ______ rations: a few ounces of dried meat and a handful of biscuits had to sustain each member through days of grueling travel.

choices.why: Copious means plentiful and abundant, the opposite of the tiny quantities the colon lists.
Negligible means so small as to be unimportant, but these barely sufficient rations mattered greatly to survival.
'A few ounces... and a handful... had to sustain each member' for weeks signals scarce, inadequate supply, which is meager.
Perishable means prone to spoiling, which addresses freshness rather than the quantity the passage emphasizes.

stem: Unlike a novel, which invents its characters, or a biography, which studies its subject from the outside, a ______ recounts events the writer personally lived through, filtered entirely by the author's own recollection.

choices.why: A pamphlet is a short persuasive tract, the wrong genre for a personal life account.
A synopsis is a brief summary of any work and need not be personal or lived through.
A depiction is any representation; it lacks the first-person, lived-experience element the passage requires.
The contrast with novel and biography plus 'recounts events the writer personally lived through... the author's own recollection' defines a memoir.

stem: Under the electron microscope, structures invisible to the naked eye come into focus; the researcher measured ______ pores in the cell membrane, each only a few nanometers across.

choices.why: 'Invisible to the naked eye' and 'each only a few nanometers across' establish extremely small size, exactly minuscule.
Negligible stresses being too unimportant to count, but these pores are the important object of study, not insignificant.
Colossal means enormous, the opposite of nanometer-scale pores.
Intricate describes complexity of structure, not size, which is the dimension the clue measures.

stem: The playwright's later protagonists grow increasingly ______: they withdraw from society, sneer at every act of kindness, and voice a bitter conviction that human beings are fundamentally selfish and beyond redemption.

choices.why: Benevolent means kindly and well-meaning toward others, the opposite of sneering contempt for humanity.
Withdrawing from society, sneering at kindness, and believing people are fundamentally selfish define the distrust of humanity that is misanthropic.
Eccentric means merely unconventional or odd and says nothing about hating people.
Indifferent means apathetic or neutral, too weak for the active bitterness and contempt described.

stem: Coastal engineers plant dense mangrove forests along vulnerable shorelines not to stop storms altogether, an impossible goal, but to ______ their destructive force: the tangled roots absorb wave energy and blunt the worst of the flooding.

choices.why: Exacerbate means to worsen, the opposite of absorbing wave energy and blunting the flooding.
Preclude means to prevent entirely, but the passage explicitly rules that out with 'not to stop storms altogether.'
The contrast 'not to stop storms... but to' plus 'absorb wave energy and blunt the worst' matches mitigate, to lessen or alleviate.
Rationalize means to justify or explain away; it belongs to the domain of argument, not reducing physical harm.

stem: Historians of science regard the 1919 eclipse expedition as a ______ event: by confirming Einstein's prediction that gravity bends light, it overturned centuries of Newtonian assumption and reshaped the course of physics.

choices.why: Inconsequential means trivial and unimportant, the opposite of overturning centuries of assumption.
Coincidental means occurring by chance; the passage emphasizes deliberate impact, not accident.
Conspicuous means highly visible or noticeable, which is not the same as being historically important.
'Overturned centuries of Newtonian assumption and reshaped the course of physics' marks the event as significant and important, i.e., momentous.

stem: Streaming platforms initially offered their libraries free of charge, but investors soon demanded a strategy for ______ the vast audiences they had attracted: turning millions of casual listeners into a reliable source of revenue through subscriptions and targeted ads.

choices.why: The colon's elaboration 'turning millions of casual listeners into a reliable source of revenue' is exactly monetizing, generating revenue from something.
Cataloging means organizing items into an ordered list, which is unrelated to earning income from an audience.
Appraising means assessing the value of something; evaluation is not the same as generating revenue.
Subsidizing means funding something at a loss, the opposite of drawing revenue from the audience.

stem: To compress years of the boxer's training into ninety seconds, the director relied on a ______: rapid cuts of predawn runs, sparring sessions, and dripping sweat were spliced together into one seamless, propulsive sequence.

choices.why: A caricature is an exaggerated comic portrait, the wrong medium and technique for edited film.
'Rapid cuts... spliced together into one seamless sequence' is the film-editing technique of assembling separate shots, i.e., a montage.
A tableau is a single frozen, static scene, the opposite of the rapidly edited motion described.
A synopsis is a plot summary, a description of content rather than an editing technique.

stem: When Darwin compared the beaks of finches across the Galapagos, he was making a ______ observation: the birds differed not in behavior or habitat alone but in the very shape and structure of their bodies.

choices.why: Behavioral concerns conduct, which the passage explicitly sets aside with 'not in behavior... alone.'
Incidental means minor or occurring by chance, unsupported by a passage stressing physical form.
'The very shape and structure of their bodies' defines an observation about form and structure, i.e., morphological.
Physiological concerns how organisms function, whereas the clue emphasizes shape and structure, not function.

stem: Peering through the new telescope, the astronomers were staggered by what earlier instruments had missed: where the old star charts showed only a scattering of points, the upgraded lens revealed ______ galaxies, too numerous to count, strewn across a patch of sky no wider than a thumbnail.

choices.why: Scarce means few and hard to find, the opposite of galaxies too numerous to count.
Discernible means barely perceptible; it addresses visibility rather than the sheer number the clue names.
Uniform means all identical, describing sameness rather than the quantity the passage emphasizes.
The appositive 'too numerous to count, strewn across' establishes countless quantity, exactly myriad.

stem: The mass strandings of otherwise healthy pilot whales on Tasmanian beaches remain ______ to marine biologists: despite decades of research into sonar interference, geomagnetic anomalies, and social bonding, no theory adequately explains why the animals repeatedly beach themselves.

choices.why: Reversed: predictable means able to be foreseen or explained in advance, but the colon elaboration says no theory adequately explains the strandings.
Detrimental means harmful; strandings do harm whales, but the clue concerns the failure of explanation, not damage, so harm is beside the point.
The colon introduces the decisive clue—'no theory adequately explains'—so the blank must mean perplexing or impossible to account for.
Nebulous means vague or hazy in form; the strandings themselves are precisely documented events—it is their cause, not their outline, that resists understanding.

stem: In its earliest anthropological formulations, the concept of 'culture' was notoriously ______: scholars invoked the term constantly yet defined it so loosely that one 1952 survey catalogued more than 150 competing, often contradictory definitions.

choices.why: The colon supplies the clue—defined 'so loosely' that 150 contradictory definitions coexisted—so the blank must mean vague and ill-defined.
Reversed: precise means exactly and clearly defined, the opposite of a term with 150 loose, contradictory definitions.
Obscure means little known, but the passage says scholars 'invoked the term constantly'—the concept was famous, just poorly defined.
Obsolete means outdated and no longer in use; nothing in the passage suggests the concept had fallen out of use—quite the contrary.

stem: Since no repair mission can reach the James Webb Space Telescope at its station nearly a million miles from Earth, any component failure after launch would ______ working around the damaged instrument permanently; engineers therefore subjected every part to exhaustive testing before liftoff.

choices.why: Reversed: preclude means to prevent or rule out, but the impossibility of repair makes workarounds unavoidable, not impossible.
Too weak: encourage means to promote as one option among several, but with no repair possible, a workaround is the only option—compulsory, not merely favored.
Nullify means to cancel or invalidate; a failure cannot invalidate the workaround that responds to it, and nothing in the passage involves canceling.
Because 'no repair mission can reach' the telescope, a failure would make workarounds required—necessitate captures that forced consequence.

stem: Economists caution that inflation can quietly undo a raise: a 4 percent salary increase paired with 4 percent annual inflation leaves purchasing power exactly where it began, effectively ______ the gain that workers believe they have secured.

choices.why: Reversed: bolstering means strengthening or reinforcing, but the passage describes the raise being canceled out, not enhanced.
Purchasing power ends 'exactly where it began,' so the raise is fully canceled out—precisely what negating means.
Intensity mismatch: diminishing means partially reducing, but a gain that leaves purchasing power 'exactly where it began' is wholly erased, not merely lessened.
Quantifying means measuring in numerical terms; measuring the gain would not cancel it, and the passage describes erasure, not measurement.

stem: For decades after her death in 1960, Zora Neale Hurston's fiction was largely ______ by critics and publishers alike; only after Alice Walker's 1975 essay rekindled interest did her novels return to print and enter the American literary canon.

choices.why: Reversed: celebrated means widely praised, but the books were out of print and interest had to be 'rekindled'—the opposite of acclaim.
Parodied means mocked through imitation; nothing in the passage describes satire—only an absence of attention.
The clue that interest had to be 'rekindled' before her novels could 'return to print' shows the work went ignored and uncared for—neglected.
Too strong and narrow: suppressed implies deliberate prohibition or censorship, but the passage describes passive inattention, not an active campaign against the books.

stem: In the yearlong clinical trial, the supplement's effect on cholesterol proved ______: participants' readings fell by less than one percent on average, a change the statisticians deemed indistinguishable from normal day-to-day fluctuation.

choices.why: A change 'indistinguishable from normal day-to-day fluctuation' is too small to matter at all—exactly what negligible means.
Reversed: substantial means considerable in size or importance, but the effect was under one percent and statistically invisible.
Precision failure: modest implies a small but genuine effect, yet the passage says the change could not be told apart from random noise—effectively no effect at all.
Erratic means inconsistent or unpredictable; the passage describes the effect's tiny size, not any irregularity in the results.

stem: The city's pledge of carbon neutrality by 2040 remains largely ______: the goal appears in speeches and planning documents, but no budget, timeline, or enforcement mechanism yet exists to convert it into practice.

choices.why: Reversed: operational means actually functioning in practice, but the passage stresses that nothing yet exists 'to convert it into practice.'
Ambitious describes the scale of a goal; the contrast here is between existing on paper and existing in practice, not between bold and timid aims.
Unpopular means widely disliked; the passage says nothing about public opposition to the pledge.
A goal that exists only 'in speeches and planning documents' with no budget or mechanism is theoretical rather than real—notional.

stem: When Cubist canvases were first exhibited in Paris, critics recognized the style as genuinely ______: rather than refining the perspective techniques inherited from the Renaissance, Picasso and Braque fragmented their subjects in ways no European tradition had anticipated.

choices.why: Reversed: conventional means following established practice, but the painters broke with inherited techniques in unanticipated ways.
The contrast marker 'rather than refining' inherited techniques, plus 'no European tradition had anticipated,' demands a word meaning wholly new—novel.
Precision failure: modern merely means of recent times—true of all art then being made; the clue requires something unprecedented, not just current.
Controversial means provoking dispute; the passage never mentions outrage or disagreement, only the unprecedented nature of the approach.

stem: Consumer researchers find that a gadget's ______ can drive early sales but rarely sustains them: shoppers initially flock to devices unlike anything they have seen, yet that appeal evaporates once the products become commonplace.

choices.why: Ingenuity means cleverness of design, which would not evaporate merely because a product becomes commonplace; the fading quality is unfamiliarity, not skill.
Durability means ability to withstand wear; nothing in the passage concerns how long the gadgets last physically.
The clues 'unlike anything they have seen' and appeal that fades 'once the products become commonplace' point to newness itself—novelty.
Notoriety means fame for something bad; the passage describes attraction to unfamiliar devices, not a scandalous reputation.

stem: Recent biographies of Thomas Jefferson offer a far more ______ portrait than earlier hagiographies did: instead of casting him simply as hero or hypocrite, they trace how his egalitarian ideals coexisted, often uneasily, with his lifelong practice of enslavement.

choices.why: The contrast with casting him 'simply as hero or hypocrite' and the tracing of uneasy coexisting truths signal fine distinctions—a nuanced portrait.
Reversed: simplistic means oversimplified, which describes the crude hero-or-hypocrite framings the new biographies reject.
Too narrow: critical implies one-directional condemnation, but the passage rules out portraying Jefferson 'simply as... hypocrite' any more than as hero.
Definitive means authoritative and final; the contrast in the passage is between subtlety and simplicity, not between complete and incomplete accounts.

stem: In 1832, South Carolina asserted a state's power to ______ federal tariff acts within its borders, declaring them void and unenforceable; President Jackson countered that no single state could erase a law passed by Congress.

choices.why: Reversed: ratify means to formally approve, but the state was declaring the acts 'void and unenforceable,' not endorsing them.
Amend means to revise a law's wording; the passage describes wholesale invalidation—declaring the acts void—not editing them.
Precision failure: suspend means to halt temporarily, but 'void and unenforceable' and Jackson's word 'erase' indicate permanent invalidation.
The appositive clue 'declaring them void and unenforceable' defines the blank: to cancel a law's legal force is to nullify it.

stem: Sheepdog trials reward animals that are unfailingly ______: a champion border collie will abandon its own pursuit of a straying ewe the instant its handler whistles a contrary command, deferring wholly to the human's judgment.

choices.why: Reversed: independent means acting on one's own judgment, but the dog abandons its own pursuit and defers 'wholly to the human's judgment.'
The colon's example—instantly following a contrary command and 'deferring wholly' to the handler—defines compliance with authority: obedient.
Clever means skilled at independent problem-solving; the passage prizes the dog for setting aside its own judgment, not for exercising it.
Energetic means full of vigor; nothing in the passage concerns stamina—the clue is about responding to commands.

stem: Jane Austen draws much of her comedy from her characters' ______: Emma Woodhouse, for instance, busily arranges other people's marriages while remaining entirely unaware of the romantic attachments forming in front of her, including her own.

choices.why: Reversed: perceptiveness means keen awareness, but Emma remains 'entirely unaware' of what is happening in front of her.
Indifference means lack of concern; Emma is intensely invested in others' romances—her failure is one of perception, not of caring.
The colon's example—Emma 'remaining entirely unaware' of attachments forming before her—directly glosses obliviousness, a failure to notice.
Vanity means excessive pride in oneself; even if true of Emma, pride does not explain her failing to notice the romances around her.

stem: Cuttlefish can ______ their outlines within seconds: by rippling shifting patterns of pigment across their skin, they blur the border between body and background until predators can no longer tell where the animal ends and the seafloor begins.

choices.why: The colon explains the blank: blurring the border until predators 'can no longer tell where the animal ends' means hiding or concealing the outline—obscuring it.
Reversed: reveal means to make visible, but the pigment display makes the outline impossible for predators to detect.
Too narrow: darken names one specific color change, but the clue is about making the outline indistinct, not making it darker.
Replicate means to copy exactly; duplicating an outline is not the same as blurring it into the background, and nothing describes copying.

stem: Roman augurs treated the natural world as a text to be deciphered: comets, lightning strikes, and the flight paths of birds were scrutinized as ______ of coming political fortune, powerful enough to delay elections or unnerve generals.

choices.why: Precision failure: symptoms are signs of a condition that already exists, but the passage concerns forecasts 'of coming political fortune.'
The augurs read these events as foretelling upheaval, not producing it; nothing suggests comets were thought to make political fortune happen.
Reversed in time: remnants are leftover traces of the past, but the events were read as pointing toward what was 'coming.'
Natural events 'scrutinized as' signs 'of coming political fortune' are prophetic warnings—omens.

stem: Although the eruption that created Iceland's Surtsey island ceased in 1967, scientific study of the site is very much ______: researchers still return every summer to record how plants, seabirds, and insects continue to colonize the young volcanic terrain.

choices.why: Reversed: concluded means finished, but researchers 'still return every summer' and colonization 'continue[s]'—the work is unfinished.
The contrast marker 'Although the eruption... ceased' plus 'still return' and 'continue' shows the study persists—ongoing.
Notional means existing only in theory, but the fieldwork actually happens each summer; the research is real, not hypothetical.
Precision failure: preliminary implies introductory groundwork before the main effort, but six decades of annual observation is the main research itself.

stem: Critics of the regulatory agency complained that its rulemaking process was ______: decisions emerged from closed-door sessions without published rationales, leaving even seasoned observers unable to explain why one proposal advanced while a nearly identical one failed.

choices.why: Reversed: transparent means open and easy to understand, but the colon elaborates a process no one can see into or explain.
Meticulous means extremely careful about details; the passage criticizes the process's secrecy and unexplainability, not its level of care.
The colon introduces the elaboration — closed-door sessions, no published rationales, observers 'unable to explain' outcomes — so the blank must mean impossible to see through or understand.
Outmoded means old-fashioned or obsolete; nothing in the passage concerns the process being out of date, only its being hidden and inscrutable.

stem: Although the 1966 preservation statute has been amended repeatedly, its central provision remains ______: municipal courts still apply its original review standard whenever a landmark building is threatened with demolition.

choices.why: The colon's elaboration — courts 'still apply' the original standard — shows the provision is in effect and functioning, exactly what operative means.
Reversed: an ornamental provision would exist for show without practical effect, but courts actively enforce this one.
Provisional means temporary or arranged for the time being; a standard applied continuously since 1966 is the opposite of a stopgap, and nothing suggests it awaits replacement.
Reversed: obsolete means no longer in use, which directly contradicts the clue that courts still apply the standard.

stem: Restoration architects concluded that the villa's exterior colonnade is purely ______: the slender columns bear no structural load and were installed solely to evoke the grandeur of classical temples.

choices.why: Reversed: functional means serving a practical purpose, but the columns bear no load and exist only for appearance.
Antiquated means old-fashioned or outdated; the colon explains the columns' purpose (decoration), not their age or datedness.
Monumental means massive or imposing in scale; the passage describes 'slender' columns and concerns why they were added, not how large they are.
The colon elaborates the blank: the columns carry no structural load and were installed 'solely to evoke' grandeur — that is, they are purely decorative.

stem: Drawing on six decades of banding records from coastal observatories, the ______ demonstrated that Arctic terns adjust their migratory routes in response to shifting wind patterns, a finding that revised long-held assumptions about avian navigation.

choices.why: Wind patterns figure in the finding, but a meteorologist studies weather itself; the research here — banding birds and tracking tern migration — is the work of a bird specialist.
Every clue is bird-specific — banding records, Arctic terns, migratory routes, avian navigation — so the researcher must be an expert who studies birds.
Too broad: a naturalist studies the natural world generally, while the passage's exclusively bird-centered evidence calls for the more precise term for a bird specialist.
An entomologist studies insects; nothing in the passage involves insects, only birds.

stem: Rather than embrace the experimental pedagogies gaining favor elsewhere, the conservatory's faculty maintained a defiantly ______ curriculum, assigning the same sequence of scale exercises and counterpoint drills that instructors have required of students for more than a century.

choices.why: Reversed: innovative means introducing new methods — exactly the 'experimental pedagogies' the faculty refuses to embrace.
The drills may well be demanding, but the contrast is between experimental methods and ones unchanged 'for more than a century' — a claim about tradition, not difficulty.
The contrast with 'experimental pedagogies' plus the clue that the same drills have been required for over a century selects a word meaning conventional and traditional.
Esoteric means understood by only a small, specialized circle; the passage describes standard, long-established exercises, not obscure or secret knowledge.

stem: Polling analysts observed that public sentiment toward the referendum did not move steadily in either direction; instead, support continued to ______ throughout the campaign, climbing after each televised debate and slipping back within weeks.

choices.why: The clue 'climbing... and slipping back' after the analysts rule out steady movement in 'either direction' describes a repeated back-and-forth swing — precisely to oscillate.
Reversed: escalate means to increase steadily, but the passage explicitly denies steady movement and notes that support kept slipping back.
Consolidate means to become firm and stable; nothing supports settling into stability — the numbers kept swinging up and down.
Dissipate means to fade away entirely; the passage says support repeatedly climbed as well as slipped, so it did not simply drain away.

stem: Historians of computing emphasize that the transistor did not merely improve upon the vacuum tube; it threatened to ______ the older component altogether, rendering tube-based circuits unfit for the compact devices consumers soon demanded.

choices.why: Reversed: refine means to improve gradually — precisely what the contrast 'did not merely improve upon' rules out for the blank.
Compactness motivates the shift, but the blank describes what the transistor did to the vacuum tube — rendered it unfit for use — not an act of shrinking it.
Replicate means to copy or reproduce; nothing suggests the transistor duplicated the tube — it displaced it.
The result clause 'rendering tube-based circuits unfit' shows the transistor made the older component obsolete, which is exactly what outmode means.

stem: Veteran navigators still praise the elegance of printed nautical charts, yet most now concede that such charts are ______: once the industry standard, they have been superseded by satellite systems that update hazard information in real time.

choices.why: Reversed: indispensable means impossible to do without, but the colon explains that the charts have been superseded by newer systems.
The colon's gloss — 'once the industry standard... superseded by' newer technology — defines the blank as outdated, which is what outmoded means.
The navigators' praise of the charts' elegance is real but beside the point; the concession introduced by 'yet' concerns the charts being superseded, not their being merely decorative.
Defective means faulty or broken; the charts are described as overtaken by better technology, not as malfunctioning.

stem: Journalist Ida B. Wells was famously ______ in her opposition to mob violence: her editorials named perpetrators directly and condemned complicit officials in blunt terms, even when such candor put her own safety at risk.

choices.why: Reversed: diplomatic means tactful and indirect, the opposite of naming perpetrators directly and condemning officials in blunt terms.
Wells's prose may have been eloquent, but the colon's clues — direct naming, blunt terms, risky candor — concern her frankness, not the polish of her style.
The colon elaborates the blank: naming wrongdoers 'directly,' condemning 'in blunt terms,' and risking safety through 'candor' all define a frank, vocal critic.
Impartial means taking no side; the passage presents Wells as an emphatic opponent of mob violence, not a neutral observer.

stem: University administrators warn that if enrollment continues to ______ the institution's capacity to hire qualified instructors, seminar-style courses will give way to crowded lecture halls within a decade.

choices.why: The predicted consequence — crowded lecture halls replacing seminars — follows only if student numbers exceed hiring capacity, so the blank must mean surpass.
Too weak: rival means to come close to equaling, but mere parity between enrollment and hiring would not produce the overcrowding the administrators predict.
Reversed: if enrollment trailed hiring capacity, classes would shrink rather than swell into crowded lecture halls.
Mirror means to match exactly; nothing supports enrollment and capacity staying in balance — the warning depends on a growing gap between them.

stem: The astronomical calculations of medieval scholar Levi ben Gerson were largely ______ by later historians of science, appearing in no major survey of the discipline until archival research in the twentieth century restored them to prominence.

choices.why: Reversed: celebrated means widely honored, but the calculations appeared in no major survey and needed to be 'restored to prominence.'
Dismissed implies historians considered the calculations and actively rejected them; the passage indicates the work simply escaped notice, not that it was evaluated and refused.
Scrutinized means examined closely; work absent from every major survey received no attention at all, close or otherwise.
Appearing in 'no major survey' until later research 'restored them to prominence' shows the calculations were missed and disregarded — the meaning of overlooked.

stem: Conductors sometimes worry that a celebrated touring soloist will ______ the resident orchestra, monopolizing the audience's attention so thoroughly that the ensemble's own artistry goes unnoticed in reviews.

choices.why: Reversed: complement means to enhance by combining well with, but the worry is that the ensemble's artistry 'goes unnoticed,' not that it is set off to advantage.
'Monopolizing the audience's attention' so that the orchestra 'goes unnoticed' defines the blank: the soloist outshines and dominates the ensemble.
Orchestras and soloists do perform together, but accompany merely means to perform alongside; it cannot explain why the ensemble would go unnoticed.
Emulate means to imitate in hopes of equaling; nothing suggests the soloist copies the orchestra — the issue is stolen attention.

stem: Although Fanny Mendelssohn composed more than four hundred works, her music was long ______ her brother Felix's renown: nineteenth-century concert programs featured his compositions prominently while most of hers remained unpublished during her lifetime.

choices.why: The colon's contrast — his works featured prominently while hers stayed unpublished — shows her music was eclipsed by his greater fame, the meaning of overshadowed by.
Reversed: bolstered by means strengthened or helped by, but Felix's renown coincided with her music remaining unpublished, not with its advancement.
Derived from would mean her music originated in his fame; the passage makes no claim that she borrowed from or built on his work.
Synonymous with means so closely associated as to be identified together; her music was scarcely known at all, so it could not have been equated with his renown.

stem: Unlike earlier broadsides whose sponsors hid behind pseudonyms, the 1936 posters were ______ partisan: each named the party that commissioned it, displayed the party emblem, and made no attempt to disguise its persuasive intent.

choices.why: Reversed: covertly means secretly — the practice of the earlier pseudonymous broadsides that the posters are explicitly contrasted against.
Inadvertently means accidentally; posters that name their commissioning party and display its emblem are partisan by deliberate design.
Too weak: marginally means only slightly, but naming the party, showing its emblem, and hiding nothing make the partisanship thoroughgoing, not minimal.
The contrast with hidden sponsors plus the colon's evidence — named party, displayed emblem, 'no attempt to disguise' — requires a word meaning openly, without concealment.

stem: In 1918, health officials distributed a sixteen-page ______ devoted to a single subject—influenza prevention—printed cheaply enough to hand out at streetcar stops and concise enough to be read in one sitting.

choices.why: Too grand: a treatise is a lengthy, systematic scholarly work, at odds with a cheap sixteen-page handout readable in one sitting.
Every clue — sixteen pages, a single subject, cheap printing, hand distribution — matches a small booklet on one topic, the definition of a pamphlet.
An anthology is a collection of works by various authors; a publication 'devoted to a single subject' is not a compilation.
A periodical is published at regular intervals; nothing indicates recurring issues — this was a one-off handout for a single campaign.

stem: Economists have long puzzled over a seeming ______ in survey data: as nations grow wealthier, average reported happiness often fails to rise, yet within any single country, richer citizens consistently report greater life satisfaction than poorer ones.

choices.why: Consensus means general agreement; the economists are described as puzzled by conflicting findings, not as having settled on a shared view.
An association does appear within countries, but the blank must name the apparent contradiction between the two findings — the very thing that makes economists puzzle.
The two findings joined by 'yet' contradict each other — wealth predicts happiness within nations but not across time — and 'puzzled' plus 'seeming' signal an apparent inconsistency, i.e., a paradox.
Redundancy means needless repetition; the two findings are not duplicates but opposites in implication.

stem: Excavations of the ancient villa revealed that its single great hall had once been ______ by movable wooden screens, for archaeologists found grooves worn into the floor marking where the space had been split into separate chambers for different household activities.

choices.why: 'Split into separate chambers' and the floor grooves marking dividers make the blank mean divided into sections, which is exactly what partitioned denotes.
Consolidated means merged into one whole, the reverse of a hall broken into separate chambers.
Excavated means dug out of the earth; it describes the archaeologists' activity, not what was done to the hall's interior space.
Fortified means strengthened against attack; nothing in the passage concerns defense or reinforcement.

stem: Because deep-sea vents lie far beyond the reach of sunlight, the ______ of photosynthetic organisms there once puzzled biologists, who could not explain how any life at all endured on so little available energy.

choices.why: Abundance means a plentiful supply, the opposite of the shortage implied by 'so little available energy.'
'Beyond the reach of sunlight' and 'so little available energy' establish a severe shortage, which is exactly what paucity names.
Diversity refers to variety of kinds, but the clue is about how few organisms there are, not how varied they are.
Proliferation means rapid multiplication and increase, the reverse of the scarcity the passage describes.

stem: Infants only a few months old can already ______ subtle differences between speech sounds that adults raised with other languages no longer notice, suggesting that the capacity to detect such fine distinctions is present very early in life.

choices.why: Fabricate means to invent or manufacture; infants are detecting existing differences, not making them up.
Articulate means to express in words or produce clearly; the passage concerns detecting sounds, not producing them.
The parallel phrases 'no longer notice' and 'the capacity to detect' show the blank must mean become aware of through the senses, which is what perceive means.
Disregard means to ignore, the reverse of the noticing and detecting the passage credits infants with.

stem: When conservators finished cleaning the centuries-old fresco, the treatment produced a faint but clearly ______ brightening of the pigments: even from across the gallery, trained observers could detect the difference at once.

choices.why: Negligible means too slight to notice, contradicting 'observers could detect the difference at once.'
Permanent concerns duration, but the clue is about whether the brightening can be seen, not how long it lasts.
Gradual describes the pace of a change; the passage stresses that the change is visible, not how slowly it occurred.
'Trained observers could detect the difference at once, even from across the gallery' shows the change is noticeable, which is what perceptible means.

stem: In the historian's account, the coastal trading posts were merely ______ to the empire's economy; the true engines of its wealth were the vast agricultural estates of the interior, which supplied the overwhelming bulk of its revenue.

choices.why: The contrast with 'the true engines of its wealth' that supplied 'the overwhelming bulk of revenue' marks the trading posts as marginal and non-central, which peripheral means.
Indispensable means absolutely essential, the reverse of the minor role 'merely' assigns to the trading posts.
Central means at the core, directly contradicting the passage's claim that the estates, not the posts, were the true source of wealth.
Lucrative means highly profitable, but the passage says the posts contributed little; it never calls them profitable.

stem: Near the poles of the Moon, certain crater floors lie in ______ shadow: because direct sunlight never reaches their depths, temperatures there have remained frigid without interruption across billions of years.

choices.why: Intermittent means starting and stopping at intervals, contradicting shadow that persists 'without interruption.'
'Sunlight never reaches their depths' and 'without interruption across billions of years' establish shadow that never ends, which perpetual means.
Prolonged means lasting a long time but eventually ending; the passage describes shadow that never lifts at all.
Fleeting means brief and quickly passing, the reverse of shadow enduring for billions of years.

stem: Even after the invasive beetles were completely eradicated from the forest, the ecological damage they had caused proved able to ______: weakened trees kept dying for years, and the altered soil chemistry showed no sign of returning to its former state.

choices.why: Subside means to lessen and die down, the reverse of damage that keeps going 'for years' with 'no sign of returning' to normal.
'Kept dying for years' and 'no sign of returning to its former state' show the damage continues and endures, which is what persist means.
Reverse means to undo or turn back, contradicting damage that shows no sign of recovering.
Intensify means to grow stronger, but the passage describes damage that lingers unchanged, not damage that worsens.

stem: Astronomers first inferred the existence of Neptune not by seeing it but by noticing a slight ______ in the orbit of Uranus: some unseen mass was evidently tugging the planet away from the path that Newtonian calculations had predicted.

choices.why: Constancy means steadiness and lack of change, the reverse of an orbit being pulled off its predicted path.
Acceleration names one specific kind of change; the passage indicates only that the orbit deviated, not that the planet sped up.
Symmetry refers to balanced correspondence of parts and has no bearing on a deviation from a calculated orbit.
'Tugging the planet away from the path Newtonian calculations had predicted' describes a disturbance to the orbit, which is exactly what perturbation means.

stem: A faint scent of woodsmoke seemed to ______ every corner of the old inn; guests remarked on it in the dining hall, in the bedrooms, and even in the freshly laundered linens, as if nothing in the building could escape it.

choices.why: The scent being present 'in the dining hall, in the bedrooms, and even in the linens' with 'nothing could escape it' shows it spreads throughout, which pervade means.
Evade means to escape or elude; it inverts the idea that the scent reaches everywhere, and echoes 'escape' as a trap.
Dominate means to control or overpower; the passage stresses that the scent is diffused everywhere, not that it overwhelms the senses.
Dissipate means to scatter and fade away, the reverse of a scent lingering in every room.

stem: The village became a favorite subject for nineteenth-century landscape painters, who were drawn to its ______ charm: cobbled lanes, crooked timber cottages, and a moss-covered stone bridge that looked as though it had been lifted straight from a storybook.

choices.why: Austere means plain and severe, the opposite of the quaint, storybook charm the painters admired.
The cobbled lanes, crooked cottages, and storybook bridge all describe a place that is charmingly and quaintly attractive, which picturesque means.
Industrial evokes factories and machinery, clashing with the rustic, pre-modern scene of cottages and a stone bridge.
Dilapidated means fallen into ruin; the details are meant to seem charming, not decayed and neglected.

stem: Faced with mounting protests over the new tax, the governor offered a series of concessions intended to ______ the crowds: he suspended the levy, ordered the release of those who had been arrested, and promised to hear their grievances in person.

choices.why: Provoke means to stir up anger, the reverse of the soothing effect the governor's concessions were meant to have.
Mobilize means to rally people into action; the governor wanted to quiet the crowds, not organize them.
Suspending the tax, freeing prisoners, and promising to hear grievances are all measures meant to calm angry crowds, which is what placate means.
Disperse means to scatter a crowd physically; the concessions aim to ease the crowds' anger, not to drive them apart.

stem: Long before atoms could be observed by any instrument, Dalton found it useful to ______ that all matter is composed of tiny indivisible particles; from this unproven assumption he was then able to derive the laws of chemical combination.

choices.why: Verify means to confirm with evidence, impossible here since atoms 'could not be observed' and the idea is called 'unproven.'
Refute means to disprove, the reverse of adopting the idea as a starting premise for further reasoning.
Demonstrate means to prove conclusively, contradicting the passage's explicit label 'unproven assumption.'
Assuming an unproven idea as the basis from which laws are then derived is exactly what postulate means: to propose something as a foundation for reasoning.

stem: The abolitionist's memoir proved unexpectedly ______: its vivid firsthand testimony swayed thousands of previously undecided readers and was cited for decades afterward as a decisive influence on public opinion.

choices.why: Swaying thousands of readers and serving as 'a decisive influence on public opinion' shows the memoir had great force and impact, which is what powerful means.
Obscure means little known or unnoticed, the reverse of a work cited for decades and credited with shaping opinion.
Derivative means unoriginal, imitative of others' work; the passage praises the memoir's impact, not its originality.
Tedious means dull and tiresome, contradicting a book that gripped and moved thousands of readers.

stem: The report drew attention to the ______ of the day laborers' situation: hired only from one morning to the next, without contracts or savings, they could be plunged into destitution by a single missed shift.

choices.why: Security means safety and stability, the reverse of a situation in which one missed shift means ruin.
Being hired day to day with no contracts or savings and vulnerable to instant destitution describes an unstable, chancy state, which is what precariousness means.
Monotony means tiresome sameness; the passage stresses instability and risk, not dull repetition.
Affluence means wealth, the opposite of workers with no savings who could fall into destitution.

stem: In the traditional concert program, a short orchestral overture is meant to ______ the main symphony, easing the audience gently into the evening before the principal work of the night begins.

choices.why: Follow means to come after, the reverse of an overture that plays before the main symphony.
Interrupt means to break into something already under way; the overture comes first, in an orderly sequence.
'Easing the audience in before the principal work begins' shows the overture comes before the symphony, which is exactly what precede means.
Replace means to take the place of; the symphony still occurs, with the overture simply leading into it.

stem: Geologists have established that a long stretch of intense volcanic activity ______ the mass extinction, filling the atmosphere with ash and gases for many thousands of years before the great die-off of species finally began.

choices.why: Followed means came after, the reverse of activity occurring 'for many thousands of years before' the die-off began.
Accompanied means happened at the same time, but the passage places the volcanism before the extinction, not alongside it.
Triggered asserts causation, which is tempting, but the clue 'before the great die-off began' marks time order, not cause.
'For many thousands of years before the great die-off began' establishes that the volcanic activity came before the extinction, which is what preceded means.
